concepts.name: Displacement
concepts.explanation: Vector change in position; distinguished from distance and expressed in metres.

concepts.name: Velocity
concepts.explanation: Rate of change of displacement with time; a vector quantity with units m s^-1.

concepts.name: Acceleration
concepts.explanation: Rate of change of velocity with time; a vector quantity with units m s^-2.

concepts.name: Equations of motion (constant acceleration)
concepts.explanation: Kinematic relationships linking displacement, initial velocity, final velocity, acceleration, and time for uniform acceleration.

concepts.name: Distance-time graph interpretation
concepts.explanation: Using distance–time graphs to determine speed/velocity qualitatively and quantitatively (gradient).

concepts.name: Velocity-time graph interpretation
concepts.explanation: Using velocity–time graphs to determine acceleration (gradient) and displacement (area under graph).

concepts.name: Scalar quantity
concepts.explanation: A physical quantity described by magnitude only (no direction).

concepts.name: Vector quantity
concepts.explanation: A physical quantity described by magnitude and direction; examples include displacement, velocity, acceleration, force, and momentum.

concepts.name: Newton's first law of motion
concepts.explanation: An object remains at rest or moves with constant velocity unless acted on by a net external force.

concepts.name: Newton's second law of motion
concepts.explanation: Net force equals the rate of change of momentum; for constant mass this gives F = ma.

concepts.name: F = ma (constant mass case)
concepts.explanation: Special case of Newton's second law for constant mass: acceleration is proportional to net force and inversely proportional to mass.

concepts.name: Newton's third law of motion
concepts.explanation: When two bodies interact, forces occur in equal and opposite pairs acting on different bodies.

concepts.name: Force (definition and units)
concepts.explanation: A vector interaction that can change motion; SI unit newton (N).

concepts.name: Momentum (definition and units)
concepts.explanation: Vector quantity p = mv; SI units kg m s^-1.

concepts.name: Principle of conservation of momentum
concepts.explanation: Total momentum of an isolated system remains constant before and after interactions such as collisions.

concepts.name: Friction as a resistive force
concepts.explanation: A force that opposes relative motion between surfaces in contact.

concepts.name: Newton's law of universal gravitation
concepts.explanation: Gravitational force between two masses is F = G m1 m2 / d^2.

concepts.name: Weight
concepts.explanation: Gravitational force on a mass: W = mg (units N).

concepts.name: Acceleration due to gravity (g)
concepts.explanation: Local gravitational acceleration; can be measured experimentally and varies on different celestial bodies.

concepts.name: Density
concepts.explanation: Mass per unit volume (ρ = m/V) with SI units kg m^-3.

concepts.name: Pressure
concepts.explanation: Normal force per unit area (P = F/A) with SI unit pascal (Pa).

concepts.name: Pressure in liquids and gases
concepts.explanation: Understanding and calculating pressure effects in fluids, including atmospheric pressure contexts.

concepts.name: Boyle's law
concepts.explanation: For a fixed mass of gas at constant temperature, pressure is inversely proportional to volume (pV = constant).

concepts.name: Archimedes' principle
concepts.explanation: Upthrust on an immersed body equals the weight of the fluid displaced.

concepts.name: Law of flotation
concepts.explanation: A floating body displaces its own weight of fluid; relates upthrust to weight for floating equilibrium.

concepts.name: Moment of a force (torque)
concepts.explanation: Turning effect of a force about a pivot: moment = force × perpendicular distance.

concepts.name: Lever
concepts.explanation: A rigid bar pivoted about a fulcrum, used to amplify force or distance; analyzed using moments.

concepts.name: Couple
concepts.explanation: Two equal and opposite parallel forces separated by a distance producing a pure turning effect (no net force).

concepts.name: Equilibrium of forces (translational equilibrium)
concepts.explanation: For equilibrium, the sum of forces in any direction equals the sum of forces in the opposite direction (net force = 0).

concepts.name: Equilibrium of moments (rotational equilibrium)
concepts.explanation: For equilibrium, the sum of clockwise moments about any point equals the sum of anticlockwise moments (net moment = 0).

concepts.name: Work done by a force parallel to displacement
concepts.explanation: Calculation of work when force and displacement are in the same direction (W = Fd).

concepts.name: Energy as ability to do work
concepts.explanation: Definition of energy as the capacity to do work.

concepts.name: Forms of energy
concepts.explanation: Recognition of different forms of energy (e.g., kinetic, potential, electrical, thermal) as distinct categories.

concepts.name: Gravitational potential energy formula
concepts.explanation: Calculation of gravitational potential energy using EP = mgh.

concepts.name: Kinetic energy formula
concepts.explanation: Calculation of kinetic energy using Ek = 1/2 mv^2.

concepts.name: Energy conversions
concepts.explanation: Understanding and describing conversion of energy from one form to another in devices and processes.

concepts.name: Demonstrations of energy conversion in devices
concepts.explanation: Using demonstrations (e.g., bulbs, motors) to show energy input-output changes and identify conversion pathways.

concepts.name: Principle of conservation of energy
concepts.explanation: Energy cannot be created or destroyed; it is transformed or transferred while total energy of an isolated system remains constant.

concepts.name: Power as rate of doing work
concepts.explanation: Definition of power as work done per unit time (P = W/t) and equivalently rate of energy conversion (P = E/t).

concepts.name: Unit of power (watt)
concepts.explanation: Power measured in watts, where 1 W = 1 J/s.

concepts.name: Estimating average power for climbing stairs
concepts.explanation: Procedure to estimate a person's average power output when running upstairs using P ≈ mgh/t.

concepts.name: Estimating average power for repeated weight lifting
concepts.explanation: Procedure to estimate average power during repeated lifting using work per lift and repetitions over time.

concepts.name: Efficiency as percentage
concepts.explanation: Definition and calculation of efficiency using percentage efficiency = (power output / power input) × 100.

concepts.name: Mass-energy equivalence
concepts.explanation: Understanding that mass is a form of energy expressed by E = mc^2.

concepts.name: Measurement of velocity
concepts.explanation: Experimental determination of velocity by measuring displacement over time (e.g., using ticker timer, stopwatch and meter scale) and calculating v = Δx/Δt.

concepts.name: Measurement of acceleration
concepts.explanation: Experimental determination of acceleration from change in velocity per unit time, commonly using motion data to compute a = Δv/Δt or from v–t slope.

concepts.name: Experimental verification of Newton's second law (a ∝ F)
concepts.explanation: Demonstrating that acceleration is directly proportional to applied net force for constant mass by varying force and measuring resulting acceleration.

concepts.name: Verification of conservation of momentum
concepts.explanation: Experimental confirmation that total linear momentum of an isolated system remains constant during interactions (e.g., collisions on a track).

concepts.name: Measurement of gravitational acceleration (g)
concepts.explanation: Determining the local value of g through experiments such as free fall, pendulum methods, or inclined plane analysis.

concepts.name: Verification of Boyle's law
concepts.explanation: Experimentally establishing that for a fixed mass of gas at constant temperature, pressure is inversely proportional to volume (PV = constant).

concepts.name: Equilibrium of coplanar forces
concepts.explanation: Investigating conditions for equilibrium of forces acting in a plane, including that the net force and net moment are zero (ΣF = 0, Στ = 0).

concepts.name: Thermometric property
concepts.explanation: A physical property that changes measurably with temperature and can be used as the basis for temperature measurement.

concepts.name: Calibration of a thermometer using fixed points (ice point and steam point)
concepts.explanation: Procedure for setting a thermometer scale by assigning standard temperatures to the melting point of ice and the boiling point of water (at standard pressure).

concepts.name: Graduation of a thermometer scale
concepts.explanation: Marking equal divisions between fixed points to create a usable temperature scale for readings.

concepts.name: Liquid-in-glass thermometer principle (length of liquid column)
concepts.explanation: Using the change in length of a liquid column (e.g., mercury) due to thermal expansion as a measure of temperature.

concepts.name: Thermocouple thermometer (emf-temperature relationship)
concepts.explanation: Using the thermoelectric emf generated by junctions of two different metals as a measure of temperature.

concepts.name: Resistance thermometer (resistance-temperature relationship)
concepts.explanation: Using the change in electrical resistance of a conductor/sensor with temperature to measure temperature.

concepts.name: Constant-volume gas thermometer principle (pressure of a gas at constant volume)
concepts.explanation: Measuring temperature by observing how gas pressure varies with temperature when volume is kept constant.

concepts.name: Constant-pressure gas thermometer principle (volume of a gas at constant pressure)
concepts.explanation: Measuring temperature by observing how gas volume varies with temperature when pressure is kept constant.

concepts.name: Optical thermometry by colour change
concepts.explanation: Inferring temperature from changes in colour (e.g., glow colour of hot objects) as a temperature-dependent property.

concepts.name: Clinical thermometer
concepts.explanation: A practical thermometer designed for measuring human body temperature over a limited range with fine resolution.

concepts.name: Oven thermometer
concepts.explanation: A practical thermometer used to measure the temperature inside an oven, typically over a higher temperature range.

concepts.name: Boiler thermometer
concepts.explanation: A practical thermometer for monitoring temperatures in boilers or heating systems, often under high-temperature conditions.

concepts.name: Automobile temperature gauge
concepts.explanation: A temperature-measuring device in a car (commonly for engine coolant) that indicates operating temperature to prevent overheating.

concepts.name: Comparing thermometer readings for an unknown temperature
concepts.explanation: Determining an unknown temperature by measuring it with different thermometers and comparing the values obtained.

concepts.name: Temperature
concepts.explanation: Physical quantity representing the degree of hotness or coldness of a body.

concepts.name: Calibration of a thermometer using a straight-line graph between reference points
concepts.explanation: Procedure of defining a temperature scale by plotting a linear graph between two fixed reference points and interpolating intermediate temperatures.

concepts.name: SI unit of temperature (kelvin)
concepts.explanation: The standard unit for measuring thermodynamic temperature in the SI system is the kelvin (K).

concepts.name: Kelvin (K) as the SI unit of temperature
concepts.explanation: The kelvin is the SI base unit for thermodynamic temperature, used for absolute temperature measurements.

concepts.name: Celsius temperature scale
concepts.explanation: Common practical temperature scale where temperature is measured in degrees Celsius (°C), widely used for everyday and laboratory measurements.

concepts.name: Celsius-Kelvin temperature conversion
concepts.explanation: Conversion between Celsius and Kelvin temperature scales using the relation t/°C = T/K − 273.15 (i.e., T = t + 273.15).

concepts.name: Temperature scale
concepts.explanation: A calibrated scale for expressing temperature values (e.g., Celsius and Kelvin) based on a thermometric property.

concepts.name: Thermometer as a temperature-measuring instrument
concepts.explanation: A thermometer is an instrument used to measure temperature by indicating the thermal state of a body.

concepts.name: Thermometer calibration and fixed points
concepts.explanation: Thermometers can give different readings unless they are calibrated using agreed fixed points (e.g., ice point and steam point) to define a temperature scale.

concepts.name: Thermometric property dependence
concepts.explanation: Different thermometers rely on different thermometric properties (e.g., liquid expansion, gas pressure, electrical resistance), which can lead to different temperature readings if not standardized.

concepts.name: Standard thermometer (school standard)
concepts.explanation: Use a selected thermometer as a reference standard in school to compare/calibrate other thermometers for consistent temperature measurement.

concepts.name: Commercial laboratory thermometer as standard
concepts.explanation: A commercially available laboratory thermometer can serve as the school’s standard thermometer for temperature measurements and checks.

concepts.name: Heat capacity
concepts.explanation: The amount of heat required to raise the temperature of a whole body by 1 K (or 1°C); depends on the material and the mass of the body.
concepts.broader_concept: Heat Capacity and Specific Heat Capacity

concepts.name: Specific heat capacity
concepts.explanation: The heat required to raise the temperature of 1 kg of a substance by 1 K (or 1°C); relates heat, mass, and temperature change.
concepts.broader_concept: Heat Capacity and Specific Heat Capacity

concepts.name: Latent heat
concepts.explanation: Heat absorbed or released during a phase change at constant temperature (e.g., melting, boiling), without changing the substance’s temperature.

concepts.name: Specific latent heat
concepts.explanation: Heat energy required to change the phase of 1 kg of a substance at constant temperature; relates energy transfer during melting/boiling without temperature change.

concepts.name: Heat
concepts.explanation: Thermal energy transferred between systems due to a temperature difference.

concepts.name: Heat Transfer
concepts.explanation: The process by which thermal energy moves from a higher-temperature region or object to a lower-temperature region or object.

concepts.name: Conduction
concepts.explanation: Heat transfer through direct contact within a material or between materials, driven by particle collisions and energy diffusion without bulk motion.

concepts.name: Convection
concepts.explanation: Heat transfer by the bulk motion of a fluid (liquid or gas), typically involving warmer, less dense fluid rising and cooler, denser fluid sinking.

concepts.name: Radiation (Thermal Radiation)
concepts.explanation: Heat transfer by electromagnetic waves emitted by matter due to its temperature, requiring no medium.

concepts.name: Heat pump (refrigerator) principle
concepts.explanation: A device that transfers thermal energy from a colder region to a warmer region by doing external work (e.g., a refrigerator removing heat from its interior and rejecting it to the room).

concepts.name: Evaporative cooling in perspiration
concepts.explanation: Cooling of the body when sweat evaporates, absorbing latent heat of vaporization from the skin and thereby lowering skin temperature.

concepts.name: U-value (thermal transmittance) in domestic contexts
concepts.explanation: A measure of heat transfer through a building element per unit area per unit temperature difference, used to compare insulation quality in walls, windows, roofs, etc.
concepts.broader_concept: Heat transfer through materials (conduction and insulation)

concepts.name: Domestic hot-water heating
concepts.explanation: Supplying and maintaining hot water in a home by transferring heat to water (e.g., storage tank or instantaneous heater) and minimizing heat losses.
concepts.broader_concept: Heating systems and energy use in homes

concepts.name: Heat-related calculations
concepts.explanation: Perform numerical problem-solving involving heat quantities (e.g., calculating heat transfer using given data and standard heat relations).

concepts.name: Simple heat experiments
concepts.explanation: Plan and carry out basic classroom experiments demonstrating heat effects and heat transfer with simple apparatus and observations.

concepts.name: Heat as a form of energy
concepts.explanation: Definition of heat as energy transferred due to a temperature difference, commonly associated with a rise in temperature of a body.

concepts.name: Change in temperature
concepts.explanation: The idea that temperature can increase or decrease (rise or fall) as conditions change, often due to heating or cooling.

concepts.name: Solar constant (solar irradiance)
concepts.explanation: Definition of the solar constant as the solar power per unit area received at the top of Earth's atmosphere on a surface perpendicular to the Sun's rays (units: W m^-2).

concepts.name: Radiation from the Sun
concepts.explanation: Heat transfer from the Sun to Earth by electromagnetic radiation (energy transfer without a material medium).

concepts.name: Qualitative comparison of rates of thermal conduction through solids
concepts.explanation: Comparing how quickly different solids conduct heat based on material properties (e.g., metals vs non-metals) without requiring numerical calculation.

concepts.name: Thermometer calibration curve
concepts.explanation: Graphical relationship used to calibrate a thermometer by comparing its readings against known reference temperatures to obtain a correction curve.

concepts.name: Calibration of a thermometer using a laboratory mercury thermometer as standard
concepts.explanation: Experimental procedure for calibrating a thermometer by using a laboratory mercury thermometer as the reference standard and determining corresponding readings.

concepts.name: Laboratory mercury thermometer as a standard
concepts.explanation: Use of a mercury-in-glass laboratory thermometer as a reference instrument for comparing and calibrating other thermometers.

concepts.name: Measuring heat capacity by electrical method
concepts.explanation: Determining heat capacity by supplying a known electrical energy (e.g., using E = VIt) and measuring the resulting temperature rise.

concepts.name: Measuring heat capacity by mechanical method
concepts.explanation: Determining heat capacity by converting known mechanical work into heat (e.g., stirring/paddle-wheel method) and measuring the temperature rise.

concepts.name: Latent heat of fusion of ice
concepts.explanation: The amount of heat required to convert unit mass of ice at its melting point into water at the same temperature (no temperature change during the phase change).

concepts.name: Measurement of specific latent heat of fusion (ice)
concepts.explanation: Experimental procedure to determine the specific latent heat of fusion of ice by measuring heat exchanged during melting (typically using calorimetry).

concepts.name: Latent heat of vaporisation of water
concepts.explanation: The amount of heat energy required to convert unit mass of water into steam at its boiling point without a change in temperature (energy absorbed during phase change).

concepts.name: Doppler effect
concepts.explanation: Change in observed frequency (and wavelength) of a wave due to relative motion between source and observer.

concepts.name: Doppler shift calculations
concepts.explanation: Use of Doppler effect relationships to calculate observed frequency/wavelength for moving sources or observers (including sign conventions for approaching/receding).

concepts.name: Redshift as Doppler effect
concepts.explanation: Apparent shift of spectral lines toward longer wavelengths due to a light source moving away from the observer.

concepts.name: Speed measurement using Doppler radar (speed traps)
concepts.explanation: Application of the Doppler effect with reflected radio/microwave waves to determine a vehicle's speed from frequency shift.

concepts.name: Wave phenomena (everyday examples)
concepts.explanation: Recognition and classification of real-world wave types and behaviors using examples such as sea waves, seismic waves, and radio waves.

concepts.name: Slinky wave demonstration
concepts.explanation: Use of a slinky to demonstrate basic wave behavior (e.g., pulse/periodic waves) and observe wave properties qualitatively.

concepts.name: Ripple tank demonstration
concepts.explanation: Use of a ripple tank to visualize water-wave propagation and wavefront patterns for simple qualitative investigations.

concepts.name: Sound from a moving source (Doppler effect)
concepts.explanation: Change in the observed sound (especially frequency/pitch) due to relative motion of the source and observer.

concepts.name: Longitudinal waves
concepts.explanation: Waves in which particles of the medium vibrate parallel to the direction of wave propagation (compressions and rarefactions).

concepts.name: Transverse waves
concepts.explanation: Waves in which particles of the medium vibrate perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation (crests and troughs).

concepts.name: Wave frequency
concepts.explanation: The number of wave cycles passing a point per second, measured in hertz (Hz).

concepts.name: Wavelength
concepts.explanation: The distance between successive points in phase on a wave (e.g., crest to crest), measured in meters.

concepts.name: Wave amplitude
concepts.explanation: The maximum displacement of a point on a wave from its equilibrium position, related to wave energy/intensity.

concepts.name: Wave speed (velocity)
concepts.explanation: The rate at which a wave disturbance propagates through a medium, measured in m/s.

concepts.name: Wave equation c = fλ
concepts.explanation: Relationship linking wave speed c to frequency f and wavelength λ; for light in vacuum, c is the speed of light.

concepts.name: Reflection of waves
concepts.explanation: The bouncing back of a wave at a boundary, with angle of incidence equal to angle of reflection (for rays).

concepts.name: Refraction of waves
concepts.explanation: The change in direction (and wavelength) of a wave when it enters a different medium due to a change in wave speed.

concepts.name: Diffraction of waves
concepts.explanation: The spreading of waves as they pass through an aperture or around an obstacle, strongest when aperture size is comparable to wavelength.

concepts.name: Interference
concepts.explanation: The superposition of two or more waves producing regions of constructive and destructive combination.

concepts.name: Polarisation
concepts.explanation: Restriction of transverse wave vibrations to a particular plane; demonstrates the transverse nature of light.

concepts.name: Stationary waves
concepts.explanation: A standing-wave pattern formed by superposition of two waves of the same frequency traveling in opposite directions, producing nodes and antinodes.

concepts.name: Inter-node distance (node spacing) in standing waves
concepts.explanation: Definition of the distance between adjacent nodes (or antinodes) in a standing wave pattern and its measurement.

concepts.name: Relationship between inter-node distance and wavelength
concepts.explanation: In a standing wave, the distance between adjacent nodes (or adjacent antinodes) equals half the wavelength: node spacing = λ/2.

concepts.name: Diffraction at an obstacle
concepts.explanation: Qualitative description of wave bending and spreading around the edges of an obstacle, with the amount of diffraction depending on wavelength relative to obstacle size.

concepts.name: Diffraction at a slit
concepts.explanation: Qualitative description of wave spreading after passing through a slit, emphasizing stronger diffraction when slit width is comparable to or smaller than the wavelength.

concepts.name: Significance of wavelength in diffraction
concepts.explanation: Understanding that diffraction effects increase as wavelength becomes large compared with the aperture or obstacle dimensions (qualitative criterion).

concepts.name: Wave nature of sound
concepts.explanation: Sound propagates as a mechanical wave through a medium, transporting energy without net transport of matter.

concepts.name: Sound requires a medium
concepts.explanation: Sound cannot travel in a vacuum because it depends on particle vibrations to transmit the disturbance.

concepts.name: Reflection of sound
concepts.explanation: Sound waves can reflect from surfaces, producing effects such as echoes and reverberation.

concepts.name: Refraction of sound
concepts.explanation: Sound changes direction when its speed changes between regions (e.g., due to temperature gradients or different media).

concepts.name: Diffraction of sound
concepts.explanation: Sound waves spread around obstacles and through openings, especially when the aperture is comparable to wavelength.

concepts.name: Interference of sound
concepts.explanation: When sound waves overlap, the resultant displacement is the superposition of displacements, producing reinforcement or cancellation.

concepts.name: Destructive interference for noise reduction
concepts.explanation: Noise can be reduced by generating a second sound wave with equal amplitude and opposite phase to cancel the original wave.

concepts.name: Speed of sound in different media
concepts.explanation: The speed of sound depends on the properties of the medium and differs in gases, liquids, and solids.

concepts.name: Amplitude and loudness
concepts.explanation: Loudness is related to the amplitude (and intensity) of a sound wave; larger amplitude generally corresponds to louder sound.

concepts.name: Frequency and pitch
concepts.explanation: Pitch is primarily determined by frequency; higher frequency sounds are perceived as higher pitch.

concepts.name: Quality (timbre) and overtones
concepts.explanation: Sound quality depends on waveform and harmonic content; overtones (harmonics) shape timbre for different instruments.

concepts.name: Frequency limits of audibility
concepts.explanation: Humans can hear only within a limited frequency range; sounds above or below are ultrasound or infrasound.

concepts.name: Natural frequency
concepts.explanation: A system has characteristic frequencies at which it vibrates most readily when disturbed.

concepts.name: Fundamental frequency
concepts.explanation: The lowest resonant frequency (first harmonic) of a vibrating system such as a string or air column.

concepts.name: Resonance (definition and examples)
concepts.explanation: Resonance is the large-amplitude response of a system when driven near its natural frequency.

concepts.name: Stationary (standing) waves in strings and air columns
concepts.explanation: Standing waves form from interference of two opposite-traveling waves, creating nodes and antinodes in strings and pipes.

concepts.name: Sound intensity level (decibel scale)
concepts.explanation: Sound level is measured on a logarithmic decibel scale, allowing comparison of sound intensities over wide ranges.

concepts.name: Using a sound-level meter
concepts.explanation: Procedure for measuring sound intensity level in dB using a sound-level meter under appropriate conditions.

concepts.name: Interference demonstration with two loudspeakers
concepts.explanation: Experimental setup using two coherent sources (loudspeakers driven by a signal generator) to observe interference maxima and minima.

concepts.name: Tuning fork as a source of sound
concepts.explanation: A tuning fork produces a near-pure tone with a stable frequency, useful for demonstrations of vibration and sound.

concepts.name: Speed of sound in air (measurement)
concepts.explanation: Experimental determination of the propagation speed of sound in air using measured distance and time delay (or resonance methods) and calculating v = distance/time.

concepts.name: Fundamental frequency of a stretched string
concepts.explanation: The lowest normal-mode frequency produced by a stretched string fixed at both ends, corresponding to the first harmonic (one-half wavelength fits the string length).

concepts.name: Frequency–length relationship for standing waves in strings and pipes
concepts.explanation: How resonant frequency depends on the resonator length for standing waves, with longer lengths giving lower fundamental frequencies (e.g., f ∝ 1/L for the fundamental).
concepts.broader_concept: Resonance in Strings and Air Columns

concepts.name: Variation of fundamental frequency with string length (investigation)
concepts.explanation: Experimental procedure to vary the vibrating length of a stretched string and observe/measure how the fundamental frequency changes, establishing an inverse relationship trend.

concepts.name: A-weighted decibel scale (dB(A))
concepts.explanation: Sound level measurement that applies frequency weighting to approximate human ear sensitivity, producing the dB(A) scale used for perceived loudness and noise assessment.

concepts.name: Human hearing threshold
concepts.explanation: The minimum sound intensity (or sound pressure level) detectable by the average human ear, often treated as a reference level in decibel calculations.

concepts.name: Frequency response of the human ear
concepts.explanation: Variation of ear sensitivity with frequency, explaining why equal physical intensities can be perceived as different loudness at different frequencies.

concepts.name: Laws of reflection
concepts.explanation: Rules governing reflection at a surface: angle of incidence equals angle of reflection, and incident ray, reflected ray, and normal lie in the same plane.

concepts.name: Image formation by plane mirrors
concepts.explanation: Construction and properties of images in a plane mirror (virtual image, laterally inverted, same size, same distance behind mirror as object in front).

concepts.name: Spherical mirrors (concave and convex)
concepts.explanation: Classification and behavior of curved mirrors, including how concave and convex mirrors form images depending on object position.

concepts.name: Mirror equation (1/f = 1/u + 1/v)
concepts.explanation: Relationship between focal length (f), object distance (u), and image distance (v) for spherical mirrors using the specified sign convention.

concepts.name: Magnification for mirrors (m = v/u)
concepts.explanation: Definition of linear magnification for mirror images in terms of image distance and object distance.

concepts.name: Real-is-positive sign convention
concepts.explanation: A sign convention for geometrical optics calculations where real object/image distances are taken as positive (as specified in the syllabus context).

concepts.name: Ray tracing for mirrors
concepts.explanation: Procedure to locate images formed by plane and spherical mirrors using standard principal rays.

concepts.name: Laws of refraction
concepts.explanation: Rules describing refraction at a boundary (Snell's law and coplanarity of incident ray, refracted ray, and normal).

concepts.name: Refractive index
concepts.explanation: A measure of how much light slows in a medium, used in refraction calculations (n = c/v and in Snell’s law).

concepts.name: Total internal reflection
concepts.explanation: Phenomenon where light is completely reflected at a boundary when traveling from higher to lower refractive index at sufficiently large incidence angles.

concepts.name: Critical angle
concepts.explanation: The angle of incidence in the denser medium for which the angle of refraction is 90°, marking the onset of total internal reflection.

concepts.name: Relationship between critical angle and refractive index (sin c = 1/n)
concepts.explanation: For a boundary from refractive index n to air, the critical angle c satisfies sin(c) = 1/n (or more generally sin(c)=n2/n1).

concepts.name: Optical fibres and light transmission by total internal reflection
concepts.explanation: Guiding of light along fibres due to repeated total internal reflection, enabling efficient transmission over distance.

concepts.name: Refraction effects: real and apparent depth
concepts.explanation: Apparent shallowness of submerged objects due to refraction at the water–air boundary; connects to practical examples like fish in water.

concepts.name: Mirages
concepts.explanation: Atmospheric optical effect caused by refraction through layers of air with different refractive indices, producing displaced or inverted images.

concepts.name: Lenses (converging and diverging)
concepts.explanation: Basic types of lenses and how they refract light to form images depending on lens type and object position.

concepts.name: Ray tracing for lenses
concepts.explanation: Procedure to construct images formed by lenses using principal rays and focal points.

concepts.name: Experimental demonstration of reflection/refraction using ray box or laser
concepts.explanation: Lab procedure using a ray box or laser to observe reflection/refraction, measure angles, and verify relevant laws.

concepts.name: Lens formula (thin lens equation)
concepts.explanation: Relationship between focal length, object distance, and image distance for a thin lens: 1/f = 1/u + 1/v (with sign convention as applicable).

concepts.name: Magnification of a thin lens
concepts.explanation: Linear magnification for a lens defined by m = v/u (ratio of image distance to object distance, sign indicating orientation under a chosen convention).

concepts.name: Power of a lens
concepts.explanation: Optical power defined as P = 1/f (with f in metres), measured in dioptres, indicating converging/diverging strength.

concepts.name: Equivalent power of two thin lenses in contact
concepts.explanation: For two thin lenses placed in contact, the combined power is the sum of individual powers: P = P1 + P2.

concepts.name: Image formation by a single thin lens
concepts.explanation: Constructing and describing images produced by a single thin lens (real/virtual, upright/inverted, magnified/diminished) using rays and/or equations.

concepts.name: Optical fibres and light guiding
concepts.explanation: Transmission of light through optical fibres by internal reflection guiding light along the fibre.

concepts.name: Optical structure of the eye
concepts.explanation: Basic optical components of the eye (cornea, lens, retina) and how they form an image on the retina.

concepts.name: Short sight (myopia) and correction
concepts.explanation: Near objects seen clearly but distant objects blurred; corrected using a diverging (concave) lens of suitable power.

concepts.name: Long sight (hyperopia) and correction
concepts.explanation: Distant objects seen more clearly than near objects; corrected using a converging (convex) lens of suitable power.

concepts.name: Interference of light
concepts.explanation: Superposition of two or more coherent light waves producing an intensity pattern of alternating constructive and destructive interference.

concepts.name: Diffraction of light
concepts.explanation: Bending and spreading of light waves when they pass through a narrow aperture or around an obstacle, leading to characteristic fringe patterns.

concepts.name: Electromagnetic spectrum
concepts.explanation: The continuous range of electromagnetic radiation arranged by wavelength or frequency, including visible light as one part of the spectrum.

concepts.name: Dispersion of light
concepts.explanation: Separation of white light into component colours due to wavelength-dependent refraction (different colours refract by different amounts).

concepts.name: Colours of light (visible spectrum)
concepts.explanation: The range of wavelengths/frequencies detected as different colours in visible light, and the idea that colour corresponds to wavelength.

concepts.name: Spectrometer (principle and use)
concepts.explanation: An optical instrument used to disperse light and measure wavelengths/spectral lines using a prism or diffraction grating and angular measurements.

concepts.name: Interference colours (thin-film interference)
concepts.explanation: Colours produced when light reflects from the top and bottom surfaces of a thin film, causing wavelength-dependent constructive/destructive interference.

concepts.name: Polarisation of light
concepts.explanation: Restriction of transverse light wave vibrations to a single plane; demonstrates that light is a transverse wave.

concepts.name: Stress polarisation (photoelastic effect)
concepts.explanation: Polarisation effects and coloured patterns produced when transparent materials under mechanical stress become birefringent and alter the polarisation of transmitted light.

concepts.name: Polaroid filters and polarised sunglasses
concepts.explanation: Use of polaroid material to transmit one polarisation direction and reduce glare from reflected, partially polarised light.

concepts.name: Light as a transverse wave
concepts.explanation: Model of light in which oscillations are perpendicular to the direction of propagation, supported by polarisation phenomena.

concepts.name: Rainbow formation
concepts.explanation: Formation of a spectrum by refraction, dispersion and internal reflection of sunlight in water droplets.

concepts.name: Ultraviolet radiation
concepts.explanation: Electromagnetic radiation with wavelengths shorter than visible light; associated with effects such as sunburn and fluorescence and is strongly absorbed by ozone.

concepts.name: Ozone layer absorption of ultraviolet
concepts.explanation: Process by which stratospheric ozone absorbs much of the Sun’s ultraviolet radiation, reducing UV reaching Earth’s surface.
concepts.broader_concept: Interaction of Electromagnetic Radiation with Matter

concepts.name: Infrared radiation
concepts.explanation: Electromagnetic radiation with wavelengths longer than visible light; commonly emitted by warm objects and used in thermal imaging.

concepts.name: Infrared camera (thermal imaging) principle
concepts.explanation: Detection and conversion of infrared radiation emitted by objects into an image representing temperature differences.

concepts.name: Medical applications of infrared cameras
concepts.explanation: Use of thermal imaging to identify abnormal temperature patterns (e.g., inflammation, poor blood flow) for diagnostic screening.

concepts.name: Night vision using infrared
concepts.explanation: Technique using infrared detection/illumination to form images in low-light conditions, based on reflected or emitted IR radiation.

concepts.name: Greenhouse effect (infrared trapping)
concepts.explanation: Warming mechanism where Earth’s surface emits infrared radiation that is absorbed and re-emitted by greenhouse gases, reducing net heat loss.

concepts.name: Demonstration of the wave nature of light
concepts.explanation: Experimental methods (e.g., interference or diffraction) used to show that light exhibits wave behavior.

concepts.name: Diffraction grating equation (nλ = d sin θ)
concepts.explanation: Relationship between diffraction order n, wavelength λ, grating spacing d, and diffraction angle θ for maxima produced by a diffraction grating.

concepts.name: Demonstration of polarisation using polaroids
concepts.explanation: Experimental procedure showing polarisation by passing light through two polaroid filters (polariser and analyser) and observing intensity changes with relative angle.

concepts.name: Dispersion of light by a prism
concepts.explanation: Separation of white light into constituent colours by a prism due to wavelength-dependent refraction (different refractive indices for different wavelengths).

concepts.name: Dispersion of light by a diffraction grating
concepts.explanation: Separation of wavelengths into distinct angular directions using a diffraction grating, producing a spectrum with orders based on nλ = d sin θ.

concepts.name: Recombination of spectrum using a prism
concepts.explanation: Procedure where dispersed colours are recombined by a second prism (or reversing the first prism) to form white light again.

concepts.name: Primary colours of light
concepts.explanation: Set of three additive primaries (typically red, green, blue) that can be combined to produce a wide range of colours including white.

concepts.name: Secondary colours of light
concepts.explanation: Colours formed by adding two primary light colours (e.g., red+green=yellow, green+blue=cyan, blue+red=magenta).

concepts.name: Complementary colours of light
concepts.explanation: Pairs of colours that add to produce white light (e.g., red and cyan; green and magenta; blue and yellow).

concepts.name: Additive colour mixing
concepts.explanation: Rule for combining coloured lights where intensities add, producing brighter results and potentially white when appropriate combinations are used.

concepts.name: Electromagnetic spectrum ordering by wavelength and frequency
concepts.explanation: Comparing radiations by relative wavelength and frequency (shorter wavelength corresponds to higher frequency), including visible, UV, and IR regions.

concepts.name: Detection of ultraviolet (UV) radiation
concepts.explanation: Methods or devices used to detect UV radiation (e.g., fluorescence effects or UV-sensitive detectors) since UV is not visible to the eye.

concepts.name: Detection of infrared (IR) radiation
concepts.explanation: Methods or devices used to detect IR radiation (e.g., thermopile/bolometer or IR sensors) since IR is not visible to the eye.

concepts.name: Spectrometer: parts and functions
concepts.explanation: Identification of spectrometer components (e.g., collimator, telescope, prism/grating table, verniers) and understanding their roles in producing and measuring spectra.

concepts.name: Focal length measurement of a concave mirror
concepts.explanation: Experimental determination of the focal length of a concave (converging) mirror using image formation and mirror geometry (e.g., distant object or u–v method).

concepts.name: Verification of Snell's law of refraction
concepts.explanation: Experimental validation that the ratio sin(i)/sin(r) is constant for a given pair of media, establishing the refraction relationship between incident and refracted angles.

concepts.name: Measurement of refractive index of a liquid or solid
concepts.explanation: Experimental determination of refractive index for a material using refraction-based methods (e.g., Snell’s law measurements through a slab or liquid cell).

concepts.name: Focal length measurement of a converging lens
concepts.explanation: Experimental determination of the focal length of a convex (converging) lens using image formation methods such as the u–v method or focusing a distant object.

concepts.name: Measurement of wavelength of monochromatic light
concepts.explanation: Experimental determination of the wavelength of single-colour light using interference or diffraction techniques (e.g., diffraction grating or Young’s double-slit setup).

concepts.name: Electrification by contact
concepts.explanation: Charging an object by physically touching it with a charged body, transferring charge between them.

concepts.name: Electrification by induction
concepts.explanation: Charging an object without contact by bringing a charged body nearby and using grounding to leave a net charge.

concepts.name: Force between electric charges (Coulomb interaction)
concepts.explanation: The electrostatic attraction or repulsion between charges; depends on the amount of charge and separation distance.

concepts.name: Electric field
concepts.explanation: A region where a charge experiences an electric force; defined as electric force per unit positive test charge.

concepts.name: Potential difference (voltage)
concepts.explanation: Energy transferred per unit charge between two points; relates to work done moving charge in an electric field.

concepts.name: Charge distribution on conductors
concepts.explanation: How electric charge resides and redistributes on a conductor (typically on the surface) to reach electrostatic equilibrium.

concepts.name: Electroscope operation
concepts.explanation: Using an electroscope to detect the presence (and sometimes sign) of electric charge via leaf divergence or pointer deflection.

concepts.name: Coulomb's law
concepts.explanation: The electrostatic force between two point charges is proportional to the product of the charges and inversely proportional to the square of their separation: F = (1/4πε) (Q1Q2/d^2).

concepts.name: Inverse-square law in electrostatics
concepts.explanation: Recognition that electrostatic force decreases with the square of distance (∝ 1/d^2), characteristic of inverse-square interactions.

concepts.name: Electric field lines (lines of force)
concepts.explanation: A representation of the electric field using lines whose direction indicates the force on a positive test charge and whose density indicates field strength.

concepts.name: Vector nature of the electric field
concepts.explanation: Electric field has both magnitude and direction and must be treated as a vector quantity when describing forces and superposition.

concepts.name: Potential difference definition
concepts.explanation: Potential difference between two points is the work done per unit charge to move a charge from one point to the other (V = W/Q).

concepts.name: Volt (unit of potential difference)
concepts.explanation: One volt is defined as one joule of work done per coulomb of charge transferred (1 V = 1 J/C).

concepts.name: Zero electric potential
concepts.explanation: A chosen reference level for electric potential against which other potentials are measured (e.g., ground or infinity).

concepts.name: Charging by friction (rubbing dissimilar materials)
concepts.explanation: Electrostatic charging caused by electron transfer when two different materials are rubbed together (triboelectric effect).

concepts.name: Types of electric charge (positive and negative)
concepts.explanation: Charges come in two types; like charges repel and unlike charges attract, forming the basis for electrostatic interactions.

concepts.name: Coulomb (unit of electric charge)
concepts.explanation: The SI unit of electric charge; used to quantify amount of charge transferred or stored.

concepts.name: Conductors and insulators
concepts.explanation: Materials classification based on whether electric charges can move freely (conductors) or are largely bound (insulators).

concepts.name: Charge resides on the outside of a conductor (electrostatic equilibrium)
concepts.explanation: In electrostatic equilibrium, excess charge on a metal conductor is found on its outer surface, not within the bulk.

concepts.name: Charge concentration at sharp points
concepts.explanation: Surface charge density becomes greatest at regions of high curvature (sharp points), increasing local electric field strength.

concepts.name: Point discharge (corona discharge)
concepts.explanation: Leakage of charge from sharp points due to very strong electric fields ionizing nearby air, allowing charge to escape.

concepts.name: Demonstration of electrostatic forces between charges
concepts.explanation: Experimental observation that charged objects exert forces of attraction/repulsion, supporting qualitative electrostatics.

concepts.name: Electrostatic induction demonstration with insulated conductor
concepts.explanation: Showing charge separation and induced effects by bringing a charged object near an insulated conductor without contact.

concepts.name: Van de Graaff generator (electrostatics apparatus)
concepts.explanation: A device that produces high electrostatic potentials, used to demonstrate charging, discharge, and electrostatic effects.

concepts.name: Electric field pattern demonstration (semolina/oil method)
concepts.explanation: Using particles suspended in oil (or similar method) to visualize electric field patterns between charged electrodes.

concepts.name: Lightning conductors (lightning rods)
concepts.explanation: Protective conductors that provide a low-resistance path to ground and reduce damage from lightning strikes, linked to point discharge and grounding.

concepts.name: Electrostatic precipitator
concepts.explanation: Device that uses electric fields to charge and remove dust/smoke particles from exhaust gases by attracting them to collecting plates.

concepts.name: Xerography (electrostatic copying/printing)
concepts.explanation: Printing/copying process that uses electrostatic charging of a photoconductor and attraction of toner particles to form images.

concepts.name: Hazards of electric fields to integrated circuits (ESD)
concepts.explanation: Strong electric fields or electrostatic discharge can damage sensitive electronic components, motivating anti-static precautions.

concepts.name: Charge carriers in semiconductors (electrons and holes)
concepts.explanation: Identify electrons and holes as the mobile charge carriers responsible for current in semiconductors.

concepts.name: Intrinsic conduction in semiconductors
concepts.explanation: Conduction in a pure semiconductor due to thermally generated electron–hole pairs.

concepts.name: Extrinsic conduction in semiconductors (doping)
concepts.explanation: Conduction in a doped semiconductor where impurities increase carrier concentration.

concepts.name: n-type semiconductor
concepts.explanation: A doped semiconductor in which electrons are the majority carriers (donor impurities).

concepts.name: p-type semiconductor
concepts.explanation: A doped semiconductor in which holes are the majority carriers (acceptor impurities).

concepts.name: p-n junction formation
concepts.explanation: Creation of a junction by joining p-type and n-type regions, leading to a junction region affecting current flow.

concepts.name: Forward bias of a p-n junction
concepts.explanation: Applying a voltage that allows significant current through a p-n junction (diode conducts).

concepts.name: Reverse bias of a p-n junction
concepts.explanation: Applying a voltage that inhibits current through a p-n junction (diode blocks, except small leakage).

concepts.name: Rectification of alternating current using a diode
concepts.explanation: Using the one-way conduction of a p-n junction to convert a.c. to pulsating d.c.

concepts.name: Interpretation of diode I–V characteristics
concepts.explanation: Read and explain the current–voltage graph of a diode, distinguishing forward conduction and reverse blocking regions.

concepts.name: Ohm's law
concepts.explanation: Relationship between voltage, current, and resistance in a conductor: V = IR; used to calculate any one of the three quantities.

concepts.name: Electrical resistance (definition and unit)
concepts.explanation: Resistance is the opposition a material offers to current flow; measured in ohms (Ω).

concepts.name: Factors affecting resistance (length, cross-sectional area, material)
concepts.explanation: Resistance increases with length, decreases with cross-sectional area, and depends on the material (resistivity concept implicitly).

concepts.name: Use of an ohmmeter
concepts.explanation: Procedure for measuring resistance of a component/circuit section using an ohmmeter (or multimeter in ohms mode) and interpreting the reading.

concepts.name: Household electricity components (fuse box and meter)
concepts.explanation: Identification and basic function of common home electrical installations such as the fuse box/distribution board and electricity meter.

concepts.name: Electrical safety in the home
concepts.explanation: Safe practices and precautions when using household electricity, including avoiding overloads and preventing shock hazards.

concepts.name: Wiring a plug
concepts.explanation: Correct connection of live, neutral, and earth wires to their terminals in a plug and understanding the role of the fuse in the plug.

concepts.name: Simple fuse rating calculations
concepts.explanation: Selecting/justifying a fuse rating using basic current calculations (e.g., I = P/V) to protect circuits and appliances.

concepts.name: Electromagnets (principle and uses)
concepts.explanation: Magnetic effect of electric current in a coil producing an electromagnet; common applications in devices such as relays, bells, and cranes.

concepts.name: Making an electromagnet with coil and iron nail (demonstration)
concepts.explanation: Experimental setup using a coil around an iron nail connected to a power source to demonstrate temporary magnetism and its dependence on current/turns.

concepts.name: Light-dependent resistor (LDR) behavior
concepts.explanation: Demonstration that an LDR’s resistance decreases as light intensity increases, and how this affects circuit current/voltage.

concepts.name: Thermistor behavior
concepts.explanation: Demonstration that a thermistor’s resistance changes with temperature (commonly NTC: resistance decreases as temperature rises).

concepts.name: Electrical resistivity
concepts.explanation: An intrinsic material property that quantifies opposition to electric current; used in the relation R = ρL/A.

concepts.name: Resistors in series
concepts.explanation: Combination of resistors connected end-to-end where the same current flows through each; equivalent resistance adds: R_eq = R1 + R2 + ...

concepts.name: Resistors in parallel
concepts.explanation: Combination of resistors connected across the same two nodes where the same potential difference is across each; equivalent resistance follows 1/R_eq = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + ...

concepts.name: Light-dependent resistor (LDR)
concepts.explanation: A resistor whose resistance decreases as incident light intensity increases; used as a light sensor in circuits (e.g., potential divider).

concepts.name: Potential divider (voltage divider)
concepts.explanation: A circuit using two or more resistors in series to provide an output potential difference that is a fraction of the supply voltage, depending on resistance values.

concepts.name: Thermistor
concepts.explanation: A temperature-sensitive resistor whose resistance changes significantly with temperature (commonly decreases with increasing temperature for an NTC thermistor); used as a temperature sensor in circuits such as potential dividers.

concepts.name: Joule heating formula (W = I^2 R t)
concepts.explanation: Electrical energy converted to heat in a resistor is given by W = I^2 R t, relating heat energy to current, resistance, and time.

concepts.name: Magnetic effect of an electric current
concepts.explanation: An electric current produces a magnetic field around a conductor, forming the basis of electromagnets and many devices.

concepts.name: Chemical effect of electric current (electrolysis)
concepts.explanation: An electric current can drive chemical change in an electrolyte, causing decomposition or deposition of substances.

concepts.name: Kilowatt-hour (kWh)
concepts.explanation: A unit of electrical energy equal to the energy used by a 1 kW device operating for 1 hour; used in electricity billing.

concepts.name: Fuses
concepts.explanation: Safety devices that melt when current exceeds a safe value, breaking the circuit to prevent overheating and fire.

concepts.name: Miniature circuit breakers (MCBs)
concepts.explanation: Resettable protective switches that automatically open a circuit when current exceeds a set limit.

concepts.name: Residual current devices (RCDs)
concepts.explanation: Safety devices that disconnect the supply when there is a difference between live and neutral currents, indicating current leakage to earth.

concepts.name: Ring circuits
concepts.explanation: Domestic wiring arrangement where sockets are supplied by a looped circuit, providing two paths for current.

concepts.name: Radial circuits
concepts.explanation: Domestic wiring arrangement where sockets are supplied along a single path from the consumer unit to the last outlet.

concepts.name: Earthing (grounding)
concepts.explanation: Safety practice of connecting exposed metal parts to earth so that fault currents flow safely and protective devices operate.

concepts.name: Bonding
concepts.explanation: Connecting metal parts (e.g., pipes and appliances) to ensure they are at the same potential, reducing risk of electric shock.

concepts.name: Magnetic poles occur in pairs (no magnetic monopoles)
concepts.explanation: Magnets always have both north and south poles; isolated poles are not observed in ordinary magnetism.

concepts.name: Earth's magnetic field
concepts.explanation: The Earth behaves like a magnet, producing a magnetic field with direction and strength that vary by location.

concepts.name: Compass navigation using Earth's magnetic field
concepts.explanation: A compass needle aligns with Earth's magnetic field to indicate magnetic north for navigation.

concepts.name: Force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
concepts.explanation: A conductor carrying current in a magnetic field experiences a force (motor effect), depending on field strength, current, and orientation.

concepts.name: Electric motors (applications of the motor effect)
concepts.explanation: Devices that convert electrical energy into mechanical motion using forces on current-carrying conductors in magnetic fields.

concepts.name: Loudspeakers (applications of the motor effect)
concepts.explanation: Audio devices where a current in a coil within a magnetic field produces forces that vibrate a cone to create sound.

concepts.name: Electromagnetic induction
concepts.explanation: An emf is induced when magnetic flux through a circuit changes, producing current in closed circuits.

concepts.name: Electric generators (application of electromagnetic induction)
concepts.explanation: Devices that produce electrical energy by moving conductors or coils in magnetic fields to induce emf.

concepts.name: Alternating current (AC)
concepts.explanation: Electric current that changes direction periodically, typically sinusoidal in mains supply.

concepts.name: National grid (AC power distribution)
concepts.explanation: Large-scale transmission and distribution system for electrical energy using high-voltage AC to reduce power losses.

concepts.name: Transformers
concepts.explanation: Devices that use mutual induction to step AC voltage up or down with coils on a common core.

concepts.name: Mutual induction
concepts.explanation: A changing current in one coil induces an emf in a nearby coil due to changing magnetic flux linkage.

concepts.name: Self-induction
concepts.explanation: A changing current in a coil induces an emf in the same coil that opposes the change in current.

concepts.name: Dimmer switches (AC power control)
concepts.explanation: Devices that vary delivered power to a load (e.g., lighting) by controlling the effective voltage/current in an AC circuit.

concepts.name: Faraday’s law of electromagnetic induction
concepts.explanation: The induced emf in a circuit is proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux linkage through the circuit.

concepts.name: Lenz’s law
concepts.explanation: The direction of induced emf/current opposes the change in magnetic flux that produced it (energy conservation direction rule).

concepts.name: Magnetic flux (Φ = BA)
concepts.explanation: Magnetic flux through a surface equals magnetic flux density times area (for uniform B perpendicular to the surface).

concepts.name: Magnetic flux density (B)
concepts.explanation: A measure of magnetic field strength defined via the force on a current-carrying conductor; units tesla (T).

concepts.name: Force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field (F ∝ I l B)
concepts.explanation: A conductor carrying current in a magnetic field experiences a force proportional to current, length in field, and field strength (maximum when perpendicular).

concepts.name: Direction of magnetic force on a current-carrying conductor
concepts.explanation: Determining the force direction using a hand rule based on current direction and magnetic field direction.

concepts.name: Magnetic field due to a long straight current-carrying wire
concepts.explanation: Field lines form concentric circles around the wire; direction given by a right-hand grip rule.

concepts.name: Magnetic field due to a current loop
concepts.explanation: A current loop produces a magnetic field like a small bar magnet, with a concentrated field through the loop’s center.

concepts.name: Magnetic field due to a solenoid
concepts.explanation: A solenoid produces a strong, approximately uniform magnetic field inside, with external field similar to a bar magnet.

concepts.name: Vector nature of the magnetic field
concepts.explanation: Magnetic field is a vector quantity with both magnitude and direction at each point in space.

concepts.name: Forces between current-carrying conductors
concepts.explanation: Parallel currents exert forces on each other (attraction for same direction, repulsion for opposite direction) qualitatively.

concepts.name: Alternating current and voltage as time-varying quantities
concepts.explanation: AC voltage and current vary with time, characterized by waveform shape and frequency.

concepts.name: Using an oscilloscope to display AC waveforms
concepts.explanation: Procedure skill: connect a signal to an oscilloscope to observe voltage variation with time and interpret waveform features.

concepts.name: Transformer operating principle
concepts.explanation: A transformer uses electromagnetic induction between primary and secondary coils to change AC voltage levels.

concepts.name: Energy conversion in electromagnetic induction (mechanical to electrical)
concepts.explanation: Induced electrical energy can be generated by mechanical work (e.g., moving a conductor/coil in a magnetic field), consistent with energy conservation.

concepts.name: Inductor effects on alternating current (qualitative)
concepts.explanation: An inductor opposes changes in current in AC circuits, affecting current magnitude without requiring phase calculations here.

concepts.name: Thermistor resistance-temperature relationship
concepts.explanation: The principle that a thermistor’s electrical resistance varies with temperature (typically decreasing as temperature increases for an NTC thermistor).

concepts.name: Experiment: investigate variation of thermistor resistance with temperature
concepts.explanation: A practical procedure to measure a thermistor’s resistance at different temperatures and determine how resistance changes with temperature (e.g., by recording R at multiple T values).

concepts.name: Current–potential difference (I–V) characteristic
concepts.explanation: Relationship between current (I) through a device/material and the applied potential difference (V), typically investigated by measuring I for different V values and plotting an I–V graph.

concepts.name: Ohmic behavior of a metallic conductor
concepts.explanation: A metallic conductor at (approximately) constant temperature shows I directly proportional to V, giving a straight-line I–V graph through the origin (constant resistance).

concepts.name: Non-ohmic behavior of a filament bulb
concepts.explanation: A filament bulb shows a curved I–V characteristic because its resistance increases as the filament heats up with increasing current.

concepts.name: I–V characteristic of an electrolytic conductor (copper sulfate with copper electrodes)
concepts.explanation: Current through an electrolyte depends on ion motion and electrode processes; the I–V relationship can be non-linear and may show effects such as polarization during measurement.

concepts.name: I–V characteristic of a semiconductor diode
concepts.explanation: A diode conducts significantly in forward bias after a threshold (knee) and allows only a small current in reverse bias, producing a strongly non-linear, asymmetric I–V graph.

concepts.name: Electron as a fundamental particle
concepts.explanation: The electron is a negatively charged subatomic particle central to electrical phenomena and atomic physics.

concepts.name: Elementary charge (charge of the electron)
concepts.explanation: The electron carries a fundamental unit of electric charge of fixed magnitude (the elementary charge).

concepts.name: Millikan oil-drop experiment (measurement of electron charge)
concepts.explanation: Experimental method used to determine the elementary charge by balancing electric and gravitational forces on charged oil drops.

concepts.name: Thermionic emission
concepts.explanation: Emission of electrons from a heated metal surface due to thermal energy overcoming the work function.

concepts.name: Photoelectric emission (photoelectric effect)
concepts.explanation: Emission of electrons from a surface when light of sufficient frequency is incident on it.

concepts.name: Photoelectric sensing devices
concepts.explanation: Use of photoelectric emission or photodetection to sense light interruptions or intensity changes for control and security systems.

concepts.name: X-rays (production and basic properties)
concepts.explanation: High-frequency electromagnetic radiation produced in X-ray tubes, commonly via fast electrons interacting with a target.

concepts.name: Cathode-ray oscilloscope (CRO) as an electron-beam device
concepts.explanation: Instrument that uses an electron beam to produce a visible trace for displaying electrical signals versus time.

concepts.name: Using a CRO to display electrical signals (time-varying voltage)
concepts.explanation: Procedure/skill of using a CRO to visualise waveforms such as biological signals (e.g., ECG, EEG).

concepts.name: Cathode ray tube (CRT) demonstration of electron beam production
concepts.explanation: Using a cathode ray tube to show that cathode rays constitute a beam of electrons produced in an evacuated tube.

concepts.name: Deflection of an electron beam in an electric field
concepts.explanation: Observing and explaining how an electron beam bends when subjected to an applied electric field, indicating charge and allowing qualitative force-direction reasoning.

concepts.name: Deflection of an electron beam in a magnetic field
concepts.explanation: Observing and explaining how an electron beam is deflected by a magnetic field, relating deflection direction to field orientation and particle charge.

concepts.name: Uses of X-rays in medicine
concepts.explanation: Applications of X-rays for medical imaging and diagnosis based on differential absorption by tissues and bones.

concepts.name: Uses of X-rays in industry
concepts.explanation: Industrial applications of X-rays such as non-destructive testing and inspection based on penetration and absorption differences in materials.

concepts.name: Hazards of X-rays
concepts.explanation: Health risks associated with exposure to ionizing X-ray radiation, motivating safety precautions and controlled use.

concepts.name: Demonstration of photoelectric effect using zinc plate and electroscope
concepts.explanation: Using a charged electroscope with a zinc plate to show discharge when illuminated (typically by ultraviolet), evidencing emission of electrons from a metal surface.

concepts.name: Photocell demonstration
concepts.explanation: Experimental setup using a photocell to show photoelectric emission and resulting current under illumination.

concepts.name: Electron as the indivisible quantity of charge
concepts.explanation: Concept that electric charge is quantized and the electron carries a fundamental (elementary) charge unit.

concepts.name: Electron mass and location in the atom
concepts.explanation: Recognition that electrons have a small mass and occupy regions outside the nucleus within atomic structure models.

concepts.name: Energy units in atomic physics (eV, keV, MeV, GeV)
concepts.explanation: Use and meaning of electronvolt-based units as convenient measures of energy at atomic and nuclear scales, including prefixes keV, MeV, and GeV.

concepts.name: Thermionic emission principle
concepts.explanation: Emission of electrons from a heated metal surface due to thermal energy overcoming the material's work function.

concepts.name: Electron beam production using thermionic emission
concepts.explanation: Application of thermionic emission with accelerating potentials and focusing to produce a controlled beam of electrons.

concepts.name: Cathode ray tube (CRT) as an electron beam device
concepts.explanation: Vacuum tube apparatus that generates and controls an electron beam (from an electron gun) for observation or display on a fluorescent screen.

concepts.name: Deflection of cathode rays in electric fields
concepts.explanation: Cathode rays (electron beams) are deflected toward the positive plate in an electric field, demonstrating they carry negative charge and allowing analysis of beam behavior under electric forces.

concepts.name: Deflection of cathode rays in magnetic fields
concepts.explanation: Cathode rays are deflected by a magnetic field due to the magnetic force on moving charges, supporting that cathode rays consist of charged particles and enabling study of their motion in fields.

concepts.name: Photoelectric effect
concepts.explanation: Emission of electrons from a metal surface when light is incident, with observations that help establish the particle nature of light and quantized energy transfer.

concepts.name: Photon energy equation (E = hf)
concepts.explanation: Energy of a photon is proportional to its frequency, given by E = hf, where h is Planck’s constant and f is the frequency.

concepts.name: Effect of light intensity on photoelectric emission
concepts.explanation: In the photoelectric effect, increasing light intensity (at fixed frequency above threshold) increases the number of emitted electrons (photoelectric current) rather than their maximum kinetic energy.

concepts.name: Effect of light frequency on photoelectric emission
concepts.explanation: In the photoelectric effect, increasing frequency increases photon energy and can increase maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons; below a threshold frequency no emission occurs.

concepts.name: Photoelectric effect (electron emission by light)
concepts.explanation: Emission of electrons from a material surface when light of sufficient frequency is incident.

concepts.name: Vacuum photocell (phototube): structure
concepts.explanation: Main components of a vacuum photocell (photocathode, anode, evacuated tube) arranged to detect photoelectrons.

concepts.name: Vacuum photocell (phototube): operation
concepts.explanation: Photoelectrons emitted from the photocathode are collected at the anode to produce a measurable current dependent on incident light.

concepts.name: X-ray production by electron–target collisions (bremsstrahlung)
concepts.explanation: X-rays are produced when high-energy electrons decelerate rapidly on collision with a metal target.

concepts.name: Hot-cathode X-ray tube: principle of operation
concepts.explanation: Thermionic emission from a heated cathode provides electrons accelerated by high voltage toward a target (anode) where X-rays are produced.

concepts.name: X-ray production as inverse of the photoelectric effect
concepts.explanation: Conceptual link that photoelectric effect converts photon energy to electron kinetic energy, while X-ray production converts electron kinetic energy to photon emission.

concepts.name: X-rays are electromagnetic waves
concepts.explanation: X-rays are a high-frequency region of the electromagnetic spectrum and exhibit wave properties (e.g., propagation at speed of light in vacuum).

concepts.name: Ionising property of X-rays
concepts.explanation: X-rays can remove electrons from atoms/molecules, creating ions and enabling detection and biological effects.

concepts.name: Penetrating power of X-rays
concepts.explanation: X-rays can pass through materials to varying extents depending on energy and material properties, enabling imaging and shielding considerations.

concepts.name: Health hazards of ionising radiation
concepts.explanation: Biological risks from exposure to ionising radiation and how these risks arise from ionisation in tissue.

concepts.name: Factors affecting radiation dose to humans
concepts.explanation: How the effect of ionising radiation depends on radiation type, source activity (Bq), exposure time, and tissue type.

concepts.name: Activity of a radioactive source (Bq)
concepts.explanation: Radioactive activity as the rate of nuclear decays per second, measured in becquerels (Bq).

concepts.name: Background radiation
concepts.explanation: Ionising radiation present in the environment from natural and artificial sources, contributing to baseline exposure.

concepts.name: Measurement of background radiation
concepts.explanation: Procedure for detecting and recording environmental ionising radiation levels using a radiation detector.

concepts.name: Radon as a source of background radiation
concepts.explanation: Radon gas as a naturally occurring radioactive source that contributes to background radiation and health risk.

concepts.name: Granite as a source of background radiation
concepts.explanation: Granite rocks containing naturally radioactive isotopes that increase local background radiation levels.

concepts.name: Medical and dental X-rays as ionising radiation
concepts.explanation: Use of X-rays in healthcare as an ionising radiation source with associated benefits and exposure risks.

concepts.name: Disposal of nuclear waste
concepts.explanation: Safe handling and long-term management of radioactive waste to reduce environmental and human exposure.

concepts.name: Radiation protection
concepts.explanation: Measures to reduce exposure to ionising radiation, including limiting time, increasing distance, and using shielding.

concepts.name: Composition of perpendicular vectors
concepts.explanation: Finding the resultant of two perpendicular vectors using vector addition (e.g., Pythagoras and direction).

concepts.name: Resolution of coplanar vectors
concepts.explanation: Resolving a force or other vector into components in a plane (typically perpendicular components).

concepts.name: Force
concepts.explanation: Definition of force as a vector interaction that can change motion; SI unit newton (N).

concepts.name: Momentum
concepts.explanation: Definition of momentum p = mv as a vector quantity with SI unit kg m s^-1.

concepts.name: Centripetal force
concepts.explanation: The inward net force required to maintain uniform circular motion.

concepts.name: Angular velocity
concepts.explanation: Definition of angular velocity ω as rate of change of angular displacement; unit rad s^-1.

concepts.name: Relationship v = rω
concepts.explanation: Derivation and use of the link between linear speed v and angular velocity ω in circular motion.

concepts.name: Centripetal acceleration a = rω^2
concepts.explanation: Use of a = rω^2 for uniform circular motion (equivalently a = v^2/r).

concepts.name: Centripetal force formula F = mrω^2
concepts.explanation: Use of F = mrω^2 (equivalently F = mv^2/r) for the required net force in uniform circular motion.

concepts.name: Weight as gravitational force
concepts.explanation: Weight defined as W = mg, the gravitational force on a mass in a gravitational field.

concepts.name: Variation of g with distance from Earth's centre
concepts.explanation: Understanding that gravitational acceleration decreases with distance from Earth's centre (inverse-square dependence).

concepts.name: Circular satellite orbit period relationship
concepts.explanation: Derivation relating orbital period to orbital radius and central mass for circular orbits (Kepler/Newton form).

concepts.name: Moment of a force
concepts.explanation: Definition of moment (torque) as force × perpendicular distance from pivot; unit N m.

concepts.name: Equilibrium: net force equals zero
concepts.explanation: Condition for equilibrium that the vector sum of forces in any direction is zero.

concepts.name: Equilibrium: sum of moments equals zero
concepts.explanation: Rotational equilibrium condition that the sum of moments about any point is zero.

concepts.name: Measuring velocity and acceleration experimentally
concepts.explanation: Practical determination of velocity and acceleration using suitable apparatus (e.g., ticker tape, motion sensors) and graph methods.

concepts.name: Measuring gravitational acceleration g
concepts.explanation: Experimental measurement of g using an appropriate method and related calculations.

concepts.name: Finding resultants using force apparatus
concepts.explanation: Determining resultant forces experimentally using Newton balances or pulleys, supported by calculations.

concepts.name: Demonstrating Newton's laws experimentally
concepts.explanation: Using setups such as an air track or ticker-tape/powder timer to test motion under forces and verify Newton’s laws.

concepts.name: Standard SI units of mass, length and time
concepts.explanation: Use of SI base units kg, m, s in mechanics problems (definitions of units not required).

concepts.name: Simple harmonic motion (SHM)
concepts.explanation: Oscillatory motion in which acceleration (or restoring force) is proportional to displacement and directed toward equilibrium.

concepts.name: Hooke's law
concepts.explanation: For an elastic system, the restoring force is proportional to displacement from equilibrium: F = −ks.

concepts.name: SHM equation of motion for a spring-mass system
concepts.explanation: Using Newton's second law with Hooke’s law: ma = −ks leading to a = −(k/m)s = −ω²s.

concepts.name: Period of a simple pendulum
concepts.explanation: Time for one complete oscillation of a simple pendulum; commonly related to length and g for small oscillations.

concepts.name: Force and displacement in the same direction (work calculation condition)
concepts.explanation: Work calculations simplified to cases where force and displacement are collinear, so W = Fs (with sign by direction).

concepts.name: Energy definition (ability to do work)
concepts.explanation: Energy is defined as the capacity/ability to do work.

concepts.name: Gravitational potential energy near Earth's surface
concepts.explanation: Potential energy due to height in a uniform gravitational field: EP = mgh.

concepts.name: Kinetic energy of translation
concepts.explanation: Energy of motion for a moving mass: Ek = 1/2 mv^2.

concepts.name: Energy conversion
concepts.explanation: Transformation of energy from one form to another (e.g., mechanical to electrical or thermal) while tracking totals.

concepts.name: Average power estimation from stair climbing
concepts.explanation: Estimate a person's average power output by computing work against gravity (mgh) over time while running upstairs.

concepts.name: Average power estimation from repeated weight lifting
concepts.explanation: Estimate average power by calculating total work done lifting weights through a vertical distance over total time.

concepts.name: Efficiency (percentage efficiency)
concepts.explanation: Efficiency as a percentage: (power output / power input) × 100%.

concepts.name: Measurement of velocity and acceleration (experimental skill)
concepts.explanation: Laboratory determination of velocity and acceleration using appropriate timing and distance measurements.

concepts.name: Verification that acceleration is proportional to force
