concepts.explanation: Experimental demonstration of Newton’s second law relationship a ∝ F for constant mass.

concepts.name: Principle of conservation of momentum (verification)
concepts.explanation: Experimental verification that total momentum of an isolated system remains constant during interactions/collisions.

concepts.name: Measurement of gravitational acceleration g
concepts.explanation: Determination of g from experiments such as timing a pendulum or other kinematic methods.

concepts.name: Period-length relationship for a simple pendulum (investigation)
concepts.explanation: Experimental investigation of how pendulum period depends on length and using the relationship to calculate g.

concepts.name: Boyle's law (verification)
concepts.explanation: Experimental verification that for a fixed mass of gas at constant temperature, pressure is inversely proportional to volume (pV = constant).

concepts.name: Equilibrium of coplanar forces (laws of equilibrium investigation)
concepts.explanation: Investigation of conditions for equilibrium when multiple forces act in a plane (resultant force equals zero).

concepts.name: Angular frequency of a mass-spring oscillator
concepts.explanation: Definition and use of the SHM relation for a spring-mass system: ω = √(k/m).

concepts.name: Period–angular frequency relation
concepts.explanation: Connection between oscillation period and angular frequency: T = 2π/ω (equivalently ω = 2π/T).

concepts.name: Calibration of a thermometer at ice point and steam point
concepts.explanation: Graduating a thermometer scale by assigning fixed points at the melting point of ice and the boiling point of water (steam point), then marking divisions between them.

concepts.name: Liquid-in-glass thermometry (length of liquid column)
concepts.explanation: Using the change in length of a liquid column (e.g., mercury) in a capillary tube as a thermometric property to indicate temperature.

concepts.name: Thermocouple emf as a thermometric property
concepts.explanation: Using the temperature-dependent electromotive force (emf) produced by a thermocouple as a basis for measuring temperature.

concepts.name: Gas pressure at constant volume as a thermometric property
concepts.explanation: Using the change in pressure of a gas held at constant volume as an indicator of temperature.

concepts.name: Gas volume at constant pressure as a thermometric property
concepts.explanation: Using the change in volume of a gas maintained at constant pressure as an indicator of temperature.

concepts.name: Electrical resistance as a thermometric property
concepts.explanation: Using the dependence of electrical resistance on temperature (e.g., in metals or thermistors) to measure temperature.

concepts.name: Colour as a thermometric property
concepts.explanation: Using temperature-dependent colour change (e.g., in heated objects or thermochromic materials) as an indicator of temperature.

concepts.name: Car temperature gauge
concepts.explanation: An instrument used in vehicles to indicate engine/coolant temperature, based on a temperature-dependent sensor and calibrated display.

concepts.name: Straight-line graph between reference points (temperature scale calibration)
concepts.explanation: A method of calibrating a temperature scale by assuming a linear relationship between two fixed reference points on a straight-line graph.

concepts.name: Kelvin (thermodynamic temperature scale)
concepts.explanation: SI base unit and absolute temperature scale for measuring temperature; 0 K corresponds to absolute zero.

concepts.name: Celsius–Kelvin temperature conversion
concepts.explanation: Conversion between Celsius and Kelvin temperature scales using T(K) = t(°C) + 273.15 (equivalently t(°C) = T(K) − 273.15).

concepts.name: Thermometers measure temperature
concepts.explanation: A thermometer is an instrument used to determine the temperature of a body or environment by providing a temperature reading.

concepts.name: Non-universality of thermometer readings
concepts.explanation: Different thermometers may give different temperature readings for the same thermal state unless they are calibrated to a common scale.

concepts.name: Standard thermometer
concepts.explanation: A designated thermometer used as a reference instrument for comparing or calibrating other thermometers in a school laboratory.

concepts.name: Use of a commercial laboratory thermometer as a school standard
concepts.explanation: Procedure of selecting and using an accurate commercial laboratory thermometer as the reference (standard) thermometer for school measurements.

concepts.name: Radiation (Heat Transfer)
concepts.explanation: Heat transfer by electromagnetic waves, which does not require a material medium.

concepts.name: Heat pump (refrigerator as example)
concepts.explanation: A device that transfers thermal energy from a colder region to a warmer region using external work; a refrigerator is a common domestic heat-pump application.

concepts.name: Perspiration as evaporative cooling
concepts.explanation: Cooling of the body due to evaporation of sweat, where latent heat is taken from the skin during the liquid-to-vapour phase change.

concepts.name: U-value (thermal transmittance) in domestic heat loss
concepts.explanation: Measure of heat transfer through a building element per unit area per unit temperature difference; used to estimate and compare domestic insulation performance.
concepts.broader_concept: Thermal Insulation and Building Heat Transfer

concepts.name: Domestic hot-water heating (thermal energy supply)
concepts.explanation: Provision and storage/transfer of thermal energy to heat water for household use, involving energy input, heat transfer, and efficiency considerations.

concepts.name: Heating causes a rise in temperature
concepts.explanation: Concept that adding heat to a body commonly increases its temperature (noting this is a typical effect of heating).

concepts.name: Qualitative comparison of thermal conduction rates in solids
concepts.explanation: Comparing how quickly different solid materials conduct heat based on observable behavior (e.g., metals vs non-metals) without numerical calculation.

concepts.name: Definitions and units in thermal physics
concepts.explanation: Learning standard definitions and SI units used for temperature and heat-related quantities (e.g., temperature in kelvin, energy in joule, power in watt).

concepts.name: Thermometer calibration curve (mercury thermometer standard)
concepts.explanation: Experimental procedure to calibrate a thermometer by comparing its readings against a laboratory mercury thermometer taken as a standard and plotting the calibration curve.

concepts.name: Heat capacity measurement (mechanical method)
concepts.explanation: Experimental determination of a body's heat capacity by supplying energy via mechanical work (e.g., stirring/friction) and relating work done to resulting temperature rise.

concepts.name: Heat capacity measurement (electrical method)
concepts.explanation: Experimental determination of a body's heat capacity using electrical heating, typically using energy input E = VIt (or I^2Rt) and the measured temperature rise.

concepts.name: Heat capacity of water
concepts.explanation: The heat capacity of a given mass of water, describing the energy required to raise its temperature by 1 K (or 1 °C).

concepts.name: Heat capacity of a metal
concepts.explanation: The heat capacity of a given metal sample, describing the energy required to raise its temperature by 1 K (or 1 °C).

concepts.name: Specific latent heat measurement
concepts.explanation: Experimental determination of specific latent heat by measuring energy supplied during a phase change and dividing by the mass changed in state (L = Q/m).

concepts.name: Heat of fusion of ice
concepts.explanation: The latent heat required to convert ice at its melting point into water at the same temperature, per unit mass.

concepts.name: Measurement of specific latent heat
concepts.explanation: Experimental procedure to determine the latent heat per unit mass of a substance during a phase change (e.g., by calorimetry).

concepts.name: Doppler effect calculations
concepts.explanation: Solving for observed frequency or wavelength shift using Doppler-effect relationships given source/observer speed and wave speed.

concepts.name: Redshift (Doppler shift of starlight)
concepts.explanation: Increase in the observed wavelength of light from stars/galaxies interpreted as recession of the source relative to the observer.

concepts.name: Wave demonstrations with a slinky
concepts.explanation: Using a slinky to model transverse and longitudinal wave pulses and visualize wavelength, amplitude, and wave propagation.

concepts.name: Ripple tank wave demonstrations
concepts.explanation: Using a ripple tank to observe water wavefronts and qualitatively study wave behavior (e.g., reflection, refraction, diffraction, interference).

concepts.name: Wave speed
concepts.explanation: Rate at which a wave disturbance travels through a medium or space (measured in m/s).

concepts.name: Wave interference
concepts.explanation: Superposition of two or more waves producing regions of constructive and destructive interference depending on phase difference.

concepts.name: Stationary (standing) waves
concepts.explanation: Wave pattern formed by superposition of two waves of the same frequency traveling in opposite directions, producing nodes and antinodes.

concepts.name: Diffraction at an obstacle (wavelength dependence)
concepts.explanation: Diffraction (bending/spreading of waves) occurs around obstacles, with the effect becoming more pronounced when the obstacle size is comparable to the wavelength.

concepts.name: Diffraction at a slit (wavelength dependence)
concepts.explanation: Waves spread after passing through a slit, with greater spreading when slit width is on the order of the wavelength; used to interpret qualitative diffraction patterns.

concepts.name: Qualitative analysis of diffraction patterns
concepts.explanation: Describing diffraction effects without detailed calculations, emphasizing how wavelength relative to obstacle/slit size controls the amount of bending and spreading.

concepts.name: Doppler effect for moving source and stationary observer (quantitative)
concepts.explanation: Computing observed frequency/wavelength when the source moves and the observer is stationary using Doppler effect formulas (source approaching vs receding).

concepts.name: Standing (stationary) waves in strings
concepts.explanation: Vibrating strings form standing wave patterns with nodes and antinodes; allowed frequencies depend on string length and wave speed.

concepts.name: Standing (stationary) waves in pipes
concepts.explanation: Air columns in pipes support standing waves; boundary conditions (open/closed ends) determine allowed resonant frequencies.

concepts.name: Measuring sound level using a sound-level meter
concepts.explanation: Procedure skill: using a sound-level meter to obtain sound intensity level readings and compare typical values.

concepts.name: Wave frequency–length relationship in strings and pipes
concepts.explanation: How resonant frequency depends on the effective length of the vibrating medium (string length or pipe air-column length), with frequency increasing as length decreases for a given wave speed.
concepts.broader_concept: Resonance in Strings and Air Columns

concepts.name: Harmonics in strings and pipes
concepts.explanation: Resonant modes at integer multiples (or specific sequences for open/closed pipes) of the fundamental frequency, corresponding to standing-wave patterns.
concepts.broader_concept: Resonance in Strings and Air Columns

concepts.name: String fundamental frequency formula f = (1/2l)√(T/μ)
concepts.explanation: Quantitative relation for the fundamental frequency of a stretched string: f = (1/2l)√(T/μ), where l is length, T is tension, and μ is linear mass density.

concepts.name: Sound intensity
concepts.explanation: Sound power transmitted per unit area normal to the direction of propagation; measured in W m^-2.

concepts.name: Unit of sound intensity (W m^-2)
concepts.explanation: The SI unit for sound intensity, expressing watts of acoustic power per square meter of area.

concepts.name: Threshold of hearing
concepts.explanation: The minimum sound intensity detectable by the average human ear at a given frequency (commonly referenced near 1 kHz).

concepts.name: Sound intensity level
concepts.explanation: A logarithmic measure of sound intensity relative to a reference intensity, expressed in decibels (dB).

concepts.name: Decibel (dB) as unit for sound intensity level
concepts.explanation: The unit used for logarithmic sound intensity level, enabling wide ranges of intensity to be expressed compactly.

concepts.name: 3 dB increase for doubling sound intensity
concepts.explanation: Rule relating logarithmic level to intensity: when sound intensity doubles, the sound intensity level increases by approximately 3 dB.

concepts.name: Experiment: measure speed of sound in air
concepts.explanation: Practical procedure to determine the wave speed of sound in air using measurable distance and time or resonance/echo methods.

concepts.name: Experiment: fundamental frequency vs string length
concepts.explanation: Investigation showing how the fundamental frequency of a stretched string varies with its length (typically inverse proportionality for fixed tension and μ).

concepts.name: Experiment: fundamental frequency vs string tension
concepts.explanation: Investigation showing how the fundamental frequency of a stretched string varies with tension (typically proportional to √T for fixed length and μ).

concepts.name: Images formed by plane mirrors
concepts.explanation: Characteristics and construction of images in a plane mirror (virtual, upright, laterally inverted, same size, same distance behind mirror as object in front).

concepts.name: Mirror formula for spherical mirrors
concepts.explanation: Relationship between focal length, object distance and image distance for spherical mirrors: 1/f = 1/u + 1/v (with sign convention).

concepts.name: Magnification for mirrors
concepts.explanation: Definition of magnification for mirrors as ratio of image height to object height, with formula m = v/u (using sign convention).

concepts.name: Laws of refraction (Snell's law)
concepts.explanation: Refraction rules including coplanarity of incident/refracted rays with the normal and Snell’s law relating angles to refractive index.

concepts.name: Refractive index in terms of relative speed
concepts.explanation: Connection between refractive index and speed of light: n = c/v (or relative speed ratio between two media).

concepts.name: Relationship between critical angle and refractive index
concepts.explanation: For a boundary to air: sin c = 1/n (general form: sin c = n2/n1 for n1>n2).

concepts.name: Optical fibres (light transmission by total internal reflection)
concepts.explanation: Guiding of light in an optical fibre using repeated total internal reflection, enabling efficient transmission over distances.

concepts.name: Real and apparent depth
concepts.explanation: Apparent shallowing effect when viewing an object in a denser medium from a less dense medium due to refraction at the boundary.

concepts.name: Lens formula for a thin lens (1/f = 1/u + 1/v)
concepts.explanation: Relationship between focal length (f), object distance (u), and image distance (v) for a single thin lens used to predict image position.

concepts.name: Magnification for a thin lens (m = v/u)
concepts.explanation: Defines lateral magnification (m) of an image formed by a thin lens as the ratio of image distance to object distance (with sign conventions as applicable).

concepts.name: Power of a lens (P = 1/f)
concepts.explanation: Defines optical power P (in dioptres) as the reciprocal of focal length f (in metres), indicating converging/diverging strength.

concepts.name: Combined power of two lenses in contact (P = P1 + P2)
concepts.explanation: For thin lenses in contact, the equivalent power equals the sum of individual powers, enabling calculation of effective focal length.

concepts.name: Optical fibre light transmission
concepts.explanation: Guiding of light through optical fibres based on internal reflection principles for signal transmission and illumination.

concepts.name: Optical structure of the human eye
concepts.explanation: Key components of the eye as an optical system (cornea, lens, retina) and their roles in forming images on the retina.

concepts.name: Short-sight (myopia) and its correction
concepts.explanation: Condition where distant objects focus in front of the retina; corrected using a diverging (negative power) lens.

concepts.name: Long-sight (hyperopia) and its correction
concepts.explanation: Condition where near objects focus behind the retina; corrected using a converging (positive power) lens.

concepts.name: Transverse nature of light waves
concepts.explanation: Light is described as a transverse wave, with oscillations perpendicular to the direction of propagation.

concepts.name: Colour as a property of light
concepts.explanation: Perceived colour corresponds to the wavelength/frequency content of visible light reaching the eye.

concepts.name: Thin-film interference colours
concepts.explanation: Colours produced when light reflected from the top and bottom surfaces of a thin film interferes (e.g., petrol films, soap bubbles).

concepts.name: Interference colours in compact discs
concepts.explanation: Colours seen on CD surfaces arise from interference/diffraction effects due to closely spaced tracks acting like a grating.

concepts.name: Stress polarisation (photoelasticity)
concepts.explanation: Polarisation effects produced when transparent materials under mechanical stress become birefringent, creating coloured patterns with polarised light.

concepts.name: Polaroid filters
concepts.explanation: Polarising sheets that transmit one polarisation component and absorb the perpendicular component; used to produce/analyse polarised light.

concepts.name: Polaroid sunglasses and glare reduction
concepts.explanation: Use of polarising filters to reduce horizontally polarised glare from reflections (e.g., water, road surfaces).

concepts.name: Spectrometer (optical) use
concepts.explanation: Instrumental procedure for observing/measuring spectra (e.g., using prism or grating) and determining wavelengths/angles.

concepts.name: Infrared imaging for night vision
concepts.explanation: Use of infrared detection to visualize objects in low visible-light conditions by sensing emitted or reflected IR radiation.

concepts.name: Medical applications of infrared imaging
concepts.explanation: Use of thermal imaging to detect temperature variations related to physiological processes (e.g., inflammation, blood flow).

concepts.name: Greenhouse effect (radiation trapping by atmospheric gases)
concepts.explanation: Warming mechanism in which atmospheric gases absorb and re-emit infrared radiation, reducing net heat loss from Earth.

concepts.name: Demonstration of wave nature of light
concepts.explanation: Experimental methods (e.g., interference or diffraction) used to show that light exhibits wave behavior.

concepts.name: Diffraction grating equation (nλ = d sinθ)
concepts.explanation: Relationship for principal maxima in a diffraction grating, linking order number n, wavelength λ, grating spacing d, and diffraction angle θ.

concepts.name: Derivation of diffraction grating equation
concepts.explanation: Deriving nλ = d sinθ from path difference between light from adjacent slits and conditions for constructive interference.

concepts.name: Addition of colours (additive colour mixing)
concepts.explanation: Principle that mixing coloured lights produces new colours based on superposition of light intensities/spectral components.

concepts.name: Electromagnetic spectrum: wavelength-frequency ordering
concepts.explanation: Comparing radiations (UV, visible, IR) by relative wavelength and frequency, using c = fλ.

concepts.name: Detection of ultraviolet radiation
concepts.explanation: Methods to detect UV radiation (e.g., fluorescence, photographic effect, UV sensors) as UV is not visible to the eye.

concepts.name: Detection of infrared radiation
concepts.explanation: Methods to detect IR radiation (e.g., thermopile, IR sensors, heating effect) as IR is not visible to the eye.

concepts.name: Spectrometer: function of parts
concepts.explanation: Identifying and explaining roles of spectrometer components (collimator, telescope, prism table/turntable, verniers) in measuring angles/spectra.

concepts.name: Snell's law of refraction
concepts.explanation: Relationship between angles of incidence and refraction at an interface: n1 sin(i) = n2 sin(r).

concepts.name: Experimental verification of Snell's law
concepts.explanation: Procedure to measure incidence and refraction angles for light passing between media and confirm the proportionality of sin(i) and sin(r).

concepts.name: Refractive index measurement (liquid or solid)
concepts.explanation: Determining refractive index of a material by using refraction measurements (e.g., via Snell’s law and measured angles).

concepts.name: Wavelength measurement of monochromatic light
concepts.explanation: Determining the wavelength of single-color light using an interference or diffraction method (e.g., grating or slit-based measurements).

concepts.name: Coulomb's force between point charges
concepts.explanation: Electrostatic force of attraction/repulsion between two point charges; depends on product of charges and inverse square of separation.

concepts.name: Gold-leaf electroscope
concepts.explanation: Instrument for detecting and qualitatively comparing electric charge using leaf divergence due to like-charge repulsion.

concepts.name: Inverse-square law (electrostatic force)
concepts.explanation: The magnitude of the force between point charges varies inversely with the square of the separation distance (∝ 1/d^2).

concepts.name: Electric field strength (definition)
concepts.explanation: Electric field strength at a point is the force per unit positive test charge at that point (E = F/q), a vector quantity.

concepts.name: Electric field patterns demonstration (oil and semolina method)
concepts.explanation: Experimental visualization of electric field patterns by placing semolina (or similar) in oil between charged electrodes to reveal field-line patterns.

concepts.name: Forces between collinear charges
concepts.explanation: Calculation and direction of net electrostatic force on a charge due to other charges placed on the same line (1D vector/sign handling).

concepts.name: Charge resides on the surface of a conductor (electrostatic equilibrium)
concepts.explanation: In electrostatic equilibrium, excess charge on a metal object is found on its outer surface.

concepts.name: Demonstration of electrostatic induction using an insulated conductor
concepts.explanation: Observing charge separation in an insulated conductor brought near a charged object (induction without contact).

concepts.name: Van de Graaff generator (electrostatics demonstrations)
concepts.explanation: Electrostatic generator used to produce high potential differences for demonstrations of charging, forces between charges, and discharge effects.

concepts.name: Potential difference (definition)
concepts.explanation: Potential difference between two points is the work done per unit charge to move a charge from one point to the other (V = W/q).

concepts.name: Volt (definition)
concepts.explanation: 1 volt equals 1 joule of work done per coulomb of charge transferred (1 V = 1 J/C).

concepts.name: Zero electric potential (reference potential)
concepts.explanation: Choice of a reference level where electric potential is defined as zero (often at infinity or earth), enabling potential calculations.

concepts.name: Lightning conductors (principle of operation)
concepts.explanation: Protection method using a grounded pointed conductor to provide a low-resistance path to earth for charge, reducing damage from lightning strikes.

concepts.name: Electrostatic precipitator (principle of operation)
concepts.explanation: Device that uses electric fields to charge particles in exhaust gases and collect them on oppositely charged plates.

concepts.name: Xerography (electrostatic printing principle)
concepts.explanation: Photocopying/laser printing process using electrostatic charging of a drum and attraction of toner to charged regions.

concepts.name: Electrostatic hazards to integrated circuits (ESD)
concepts.explanation: Damage to microelectronics caused by electrostatic discharge and high local electric fields; motivates grounding and anti-static precautions.

concepts.name: Capacitance definition (C = Q/V)
concepts.explanation: Capacitance defined as the ratio of charge stored on a conductor to the potential difference across it: C = Q/V.

concepts.name: Unit of capacitance (farad)
concepts.explanation: The SI unit of capacitance is the farad (F), equivalent to coulomb per volt (C/V).

concepts.name: Parallel-plate capacitor capacitance dependence
concepts.explanation: For a parallel-plate capacitor, capacitance depends on plate area, separation, and dielectric: C ∝ A/d and increases with permittivity (ε).

concepts.name: Demonstration of capacitance dependence on area, separation, and dielectric
concepts.explanation: Experimental procedure showing how changing plate area, plate separation, or dielectric material changes measured capacitance.

concepts.name: Energy stored in a capacitor
concepts.explanation: A charged capacitor stores electrical energy related to its capacitance and the potential difference across it.

concepts.name: Capacitor energy formula (W = C V^2 / 2)
concepts.explanation: Energy stored in a capacitor is W = 1/2 C V^2 (equivalently W = QV/2 = Q^2/(2C)).

concepts.name: Capacitor charge and discharge through a load
concepts.explanation: Charging a capacitor then discharging it through a lamp or low-voltage d.c. motor to observe energy release and transient current.

concepts.name: Capacitors conduct a.c. but not d.c.
concepts.explanation: A capacitor blocks steady direct current after charging but allows alternating current due to continual charging and discharging.

concepts.name: Electric current as flow of charge (I = Q/t)
concepts.explanation: Current is the rate of flow of charge: I = Q/t.

concepts.name: Ampere definition (1 A = 1 C s^-1)
concepts.explanation: One ampere is defined as one coulomb of charge flowing per second.

concepts.name: Potential difference and voltage equivalence
concepts.explanation: Potential difference (p.d.) and voltage refer to the same quantity and are measured in volts.

concepts.name: Electromotive force (emf) as applied circuit voltage
concepts.explanation: The source voltage applied to drive charge around a circuit is called the electromotive force (emf).

concepts.name: Interpretation of current–voltage (I–V) graphs
concepts.explanation: Reading and analyzing I–V characteristics to infer behavior such as resistance, conduction threshold, or non-ohmic response.

concepts.name: Electrical conduction in metals (charge carriers: electrons)
concepts.explanation: Metal conduction explained by motion of free electrons as charge carriers.

concepts.name: Electrical conduction in ionic solutions (charge carriers: ions)
concepts.explanation: Conduction in electrolytes occurs via motion of positive and negative ions; electrode processes depend on electrode type.

concepts.name: Active vs inactive electrodes in electrolysis
concepts.explanation: Distinguishing electrodes that take part in chemical reactions (active) from those that do not (inert/inactive) during conduction in ionic solutions.

concepts.name: Electrical conduction in gases
concepts.explanation: Gas conduction involves ionization producing mobile ions and electrons that can carry current under suitable conditions.

concepts.name: Electrical conduction in vacuum
concepts.explanation: Conduction in vacuum occurs via electron emission and motion (e.g., thermionic emission) in absence of matter.

concepts.name: Electrical conduction in semiconductors (charge carriers: electrons and holes)
concepts.explanation: Semiconductor conduction involves mobile electrons and holes; conductivity depends strongly on temperature and doping.

concepts.name: Intrinsic semiconductor conduction
concepts.explanation: Conduction in a pure semiconductor due to thermally generated electron–hole pairs.

concepts.name: Extrinsic semiconductor conduction (doping)
concepts.explanation: Conduction in a doped semiconductor where impurity atoms increase majority carrier concentration.

concepts.name: Wheatstone bridge
concepts.explanation: An electrical bridge circuit used to precisely measure an unknown resistance by balancing two legs of a resistor network until the galvanometer shows zero current.

concepts.name: Potentiometer as a variable potential divider
concepts.explanation: Using a potentiometer (three-terminal resistor) to obtain a variable fraction of an input voltage by adjusting the slider position (voltage divider action).

concepts.name: Extra-high tension (EHT) in electrical power transmission
concepts.explanation: Reason for using very high transmission voltages to reduce current for a given power, thereby reducing I²R losses in transmission lines.

concepts.name: Chemical effect of electric current
concepts.explanation: Electrochemical changes produced when current passes through an electrolyte, leading to reactions such as electrolysis and deposition.

concepts.name: Applications of the chemical effect of current
concepts.explanation: Practical uses of electrolysis such as electroplating, electrorefining, extraction of metals, and charging batteries.

concepts.name: Temperature control using a fail-safe device
concepts.explanation: Use of a protective control device that safely interrupts heating/cooling operation when temperature exceeds safe limits (e.g., thermal fuse/cut-out).

concepts.name: p-n junction forward bias conduction
concepts.explanation: Understanding how applying a forward bias to a p-n junction reduces the barrier and allows significant current to flow.

concepts.name: p-n junction reverse bias (blocking behavior)
concepts.explanation: Understanding how reverse bias increases the barrier in a p-n junction so that current is very small (except leakage/breakdown).

concepts.name: demonstration of diode conduction using a bulb
concepts.explanation: Practical experiment showing that a bulb lights in forward bias across a p-n junction but not (or much less) in reverse bias.

concepts.name: Equivalent resistance of resistors in series
concepts.explanation: For series connection, the total resistance is the sum of individual resistances: R_eq = R1 + R2 + ... .

concepts.name: Equivalent resistance of resistors in parallel
concepts.explanation: For parallel connection, the reciprocal of total resistance equals the sum of reciprocals: 1/R_eq = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + ... .

concepts.name: Light Dependent Resistor (LDR)
concepts.explanation: A photoconductive resistor whose resistance decreases as incident light intensity increases; used as a light sensor in circuits.
concepts.broader_concept: Photoelectric and Optoelectronic Devices in Circuits

concepts.name: Potential divider
concepts.explanation: A resistor network (typically two resistors in series) used to produce an output voltage that is a fraction of the supply voltage, often used to convert changes in resistance from sensors into a measurable voltage.

concepts.name: Joule heating equation (W = I^2Rt)
concepts.explanation: Electrical energy converted to heat in a resistor over time t: W = I^2Rt.

concepts.name: Magnetic poles exist in pairs
concepts.explanation: Magnets have both north and south poles; isolated magnetic poles (monopoles) are not observed in ordinary circumstances.

concepts.name: Vector nature of magnetic field
concepts.explanation: Magnetic field has both magnitude and direction; represented by vectors or directed field lines.

concepts.name: F ∝ I l B (motor effect proportionality)
concepts.explanation: The force on a straight conductor is proportional to current I, length l in the field, and magnetic flux density B.

concepts.name: Direction of force on a current in a magnetic field (Fleming’s left-hand rule)
concepts.explanation: Rule to determine the direction of force on a current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field.

concepts.name: Lorentz force for a moving charge (F = qvB)
concepts.explanation: A charge q moving with speed v in a magnetic field B experiences a force of magnitude F = qvB when motion is perpendicular to B.
concepts.broader_concept: Magnetic Force on Charges and Currents

concepts.name: Forces between parallel currents
concepts.explanation: Two parallel currents exert magnetic forces on each other: attraction for same direction, repulsion for opposite direction (qualitative).

concepts.name: Definition of the ampere (via force between currents)
concepts.explanation: The ampere can be defined using the force per unit length between two long, parallel conductors carrying current.

concepts.name: Energy conversion in generators (mechanical to electrical)
concepts.explanation: Generators convert mechanical energy to electrical energy through electromagnetic induction.

concepts.name: Electromagnets
concepts.explanation: Coils carrying current (often with iron cores) produce controllable magnetic fields; used in devices requiring switchable magnetism.

concepts.name: Earth’s magnetic field and navigation
concepts.explanation: Earth behaves like a magnet; its magnetic field provides a reference direction used by compasses for navigation.

concepts.name: Kilowatt-hour (kWh) as a unit of electrical energy
concepts.explanation: Commercial unit of electrical energy: 1 kWh = energy used by 1 kW over 1 hour (3.6 × 10^6 J).

concepts.name: Household electrical protection: fuse
concepts.explanation: A fuse protects circuits by melting and breaking the circuit when current exceeds a safe value.

concepts.name: Miniature circuit breaker (MCB)
concepts.explanation: An MCB automatically switches off when current exceeds a set value; can be reset after tripping.

concepts.name: Residual current device (RCD)
concepts.explanation: Safety device that disconnects the supply when it detects an imbalance between live and neutral currents indicating leakage to earth.

concepts.name: Earthing
concepts.explanation: Safety connection that provides a low-resistance path to ground to reduce shock risk if a fault makes exposed metal live.

concepts.name: Bonding (equipotential bonding)
concepts.explanation: Connecting conductive parts to maintain the same potential and reduce dangerous touch voltages during faults.

concepts.name: Ring circuit
concepts.explanation: Domestic wiring layout where sockets are connected in a closed loop back to the distribution board, allowing multiple current paths.

concepts.name: Radial circuit
concepts.explanation: Domestic wiring layout where sockets are wired in a single path from the distribution board with no return loop.

concepts.name: Alternating current (AC) waveform
concepts.explanation: Representation of voltage and current varying with time in an alternating manner (including periodic reversal of direction).

concepts.name: Peak (maximum) value of AC voltage or current
concepts.explanation: The maximum instantaneous value reached by an alternating voltage or current during a cycle.

concepts.name: RMS value of AC voltage or current
concepts.explanation: The effective value of an alternating voltage or current, defined as the DC value that would produce the same average power in a resistor.

concepts.name: Comparing peak and RMS values for AC
concepts.explanation: Relating peak and RMS values for alternating currents/voltages (e.g., calculating one from the other for standard waveforms).

concepts.name: Using an oscilloscope to display AC signals
concepts.explanation: Procedure for observing alternating voltage as a time-varying trace on an oscilloscope to study waveform features.

concepts.name: Inductor as a circuit component
concepts.explanation: A component (coil) that stores energy in a magnetic field and exhibits self-induction when current changes.

concepts.name: Transformer structure
concepts.explanation: Physical arrangement of a transformer (primary coil, secondary coil, and magnetic core) enabling coupling via mutual induction.

concepts.name: Effect of inductors in AC circuits
concepts.explanation: Qualitative effect of an inductor on alternating current (e.g., opposing changes in current and affecting current magnitude) without using phase mathematics.

concepts.name: Joule's Law of Heating (Δθ ∝ I²)
concepts.explanation: Relationship in electrical heating where the temperature rise (or heat produced) in a conductor is proportional to the square of the current for fixed resistance and time; basis for experimental verification.

concepts.name: Experimental Verification of Joule’s Law
concepts.explanation: Laboratory procedure to confirm that temperature rise (Δθ) or heat produced varies as the square of current by measuring Δθ for different currents while controlling other variables.

concepts.name: Resistivity of a Wire Material (Measurement)
concepts.explanation: Determining the resistivity (ρ) of the material of a wire by measuring its resistance and geometric dimensions using ρ = RA/L.

concepts.name: Resistance–Temperature Dependence in Metallic Conductors
concepts.explanation: Concept that the resistance of a metallic conductor changes with temperature (typically increases approximately linearly over a moderate range).

concepts.name: Investigation of Resistance Variation of a Metallic Conductor
concepts.explanation: Laboratory investigation to measure resistance of a metal at different temperatures and analyze the trend (e.g., plotting R vs T).

concepts.name: Resistance-temperature characteristic of a thermistor
concepts.explanation: The dependence of a thermistor's electrical resistance on temperature, typically decreasing with temperature for an NTC thermistor.

concepts.name: Investigating thermistor resistance variation with temperature (practical)
concepts.explanation: An experimental procedure to measure a thermistor's resistance at different temperatures and determine how resistance changes with temperature.

concepts.name: I–V characteristic (current–potential difference relationship)
concepts.explanation: Experimental relationship between current (I) through a component and the potential difference (V) across it, obtained by measuring I for different applied V and plotting/analysing the I–V graph.

concepts.name: Ohmic behaviour of a metallic conductor (linear I–V graph)
concepts.explanation: For a metallic conductor at constant temperature, current is directly proportional to potential difference, giving a straight-line I–V graph and constant resistance.

concepts.name: Non-ohmic behaviour of a filament bulb (temperature-dependent resistance)
concepts.explanation: A filament bulb shows a non-linear I–V characteristic because the filament heats up as current increases, increasing resistance and changing the slope of the I–V curve.

concepts.name: Conduction in electrolyte (copper sulfate solution with copper electrodes)
concepts.explanation: Current in copper sulfate solution is carried by ions; the I–V behaviour depends on ionic conduction and electrode processes when copper electrodes are used.

concepts.name: Semiconductor diode I–V characteristic (unidirectional conduction)
concepts.explanation: A diode conducts significantly in forward bias after a threshold potential difference and conducts negligibly in reverse bias, producing an asymmetric non-linear I–V graph.

concepts.name: Electron
concepts.explanation: Fundamental negatively charged particle and carrier of electric charge in matter.

concepts.name: Elementary charge (electron charge)
concepts.explanation: Magnitude of the charge on a single electron (and proton), denoted e.

concepts.name: Millikan oil-drop experiment
concepts.explanation: Experimental method used to measure the elementary charge by balancing electric and gravitational forces on charged oil droplets.

concepts.name: Photoelectric emission
concepts.explanation: Emission of electrons from a material when illuminated by electromagnetic radiation of sufficient frequency.

concepts.name: X-rays
concepts.explanation: High-frequency electromagnetic radiation, typically produced when high-speed electrons decelerate or via inner-shell electron transitions.

concepts.name: Cathode ray oscilloscope (CRO)
concepts.explanation: Instrument that uses an electron beam and electric fields to display electrical signals as voltage versus time on a screen.

concepts.name: Using a CRO to display electrical signals
concepts.explanation: Procedure/skill of setting time-base and voltage sensitivity to observe and measure waveforms on an oscilloscope display.

concepts.name: ECG signal display on CRO
concepts.explanation: Application of an oscilloscope to display and analyze electrical signals from the heart (electrocardiogram).

concepts.name: EEG signal display on CRO
concepts.explanation: Application of an oscilloscope to display and analyze electrical signals from brain activity (electroencephalogram).

concepts.name: X-rays in medicine
concepts.explanation: Use of X-rays for medical imaging and diagnosis based on their ability to penetrate tissue and be absorbed by denser materials like bone.

concepts.name: X-rays in industry
concepts.explanation: Use of X-rays for industrial inspection such as detecting internal flaws in materials and quality control using differential absorption.

concepts.name: Cathode ray tube (CRT) production of electron beam
concepts.explanation: Demonstration that a cathode ray tube produces a beam of electrons (cathode rays) emitted from a cathode and accelerated by an electric potential.

concepts.name: Deflection of electron beam in an electric field
concepts.explanation: Observation that an electron beam is deflected by an electric field, demonstrating that electrons carry negative charge and experience electric force.

concepts.name: Deflection of electron beam in a magnetic field
concepts.explanation: Observation that an electron beam is deflected by a magnetic field, showing the magnetic force on moving charges and supporting the particle nature of electrons.

concepts.name: Electroscope demonstration of charge
concepts.explanation: Using an electroscope to detect the presence of electric charge through leaf divergence and to compare relative amounts of charge.

concepts.name: Electron as the elementary (indivisible) unit of electric charge
concepts.explanation: Understanding that electric charge is quantized and that the electron carries the smallest discrete negative charge (−e).

concepts.name: Photocell demonstration (photoelectric effect)
concepts.explanation: Using a photocell experiment to show that light can eject electrons from a material and produce an electric current, evidencing the photoelectric effect.

concepts.name: Energy units in atomic and particle physics (eV, keV, MeV, GeV)
concepts.explanation: Using electron-volt and its multiples as convenient units for energies at atomic and nuclear/particle scales, with correct unit scaling.

concepts.name: Cathode ray tube (CRT) as an electron-beam device
concepts.explanation: Recognizing a CRT as a vacuum tube that produces, accelerates, and steers an electron beam to create a visible spot/trace on a fluorescent screen.

concepts.name: Electron mass and location within the atom
concepts.explanation: Knowing that electrons have a small mass compared with the nucleus and occupy regions outside the nucleus (atomic structure context).

concepts.name: Cathode ray tube (CRT) components and function
concepts.explanation: Basic structure and roles of heated filament (electron source), cathode (emitter), anode (accelerator), and screen (detector) in producing and observing a cathode-ray beam.

concepts.name: Deflection of cathode rays by electric fields
concepts.explanation: Cathode-ray beam experiences a force in an electric field, causing measurable deflection that indicates the beam carries charge.

concepts.name: Deflection of cathode rays by magnetic fields
concepts.explanation: Cathode-ray beam is deflected by a magnetic field due to the magnetic force on moving charges, demonstrating particle-like behavior and charge-to-motion interaction.

concepts.name: Photon as a packet (quantum) of energy
concepts.explanation: Light transfers energy in discrete quanta called photons rather than continuously.

concepts.name: Photon energy relation (E = hf)
concepts.explanation: Energy of a photon is proportional to radiation frequency, with proportionality constant Planck's constant: E = hf.

concepts.name: Einstein's photoelectric equation
concepts.explanation: Relates photon energy to the maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons and the work function: hf = ϕ + Kmax (often written Kmax = hf − ϕ).

concepts.name: Threshold frequency (photoelectric effect)
concepts.explanation: Minimum frequency of incident light required to eject electrons from a material; below this no photoemission occurs regardless of intensity.

concepts.name: Photocell (vacuum phototube) structure
concepts.explanation: Key components of a vacuum photocell (photocathode, anode, evacuated tube) and how their arrangement enables photoemission and electron collection.

concepts.name: Photocell (vacuum phototube) operation
concepts.explanation: How incident light causes electron emission at the cathode, producing a current when emitted electrons are collected by the anode under an applied potential difference.

concepts.name: X-ray production by electron impact
concepts.explanation: X-rays are produced when high-energy electrons collide with a metal target, converting kinetic energy into X-ray photons (bremsstrahlung and characteristic radiation).

concepts.name: Hot-cathode X-ray tube principle
concepts.explanation: Thermionic emission from a heated cathode provides electrons that are accelerated through a high potential difference to strike a target (anode) and produce X-rays.

concepts.name: X-ray production as inverse photoelectric effect
concepts.explanation: Conceptual link that X-ray generation in a target can be viewed as the reverse of photoelectric emission: electron kinetic energy is converted into photon energy.

concepts.name: Bohr model of the atom (descriptive)
concepts.explanation: Atomic model with electrons in discrete orbits/energy levels; transitions between levels involve emission or absorption of photons.

concepts.name: Atomic energy levels
concepts.explanation: Electrons in atoms occupy discrete energy states; energy is exchanged in quantised amounts when moving between levels.

concepts.name: Emission line spectra
concepts.explanation: Discrete spectral lines produced when excited atoms emit photons at specific wavelengths corresponding to transitions between energy levels.

concepts.name: Photon energy from level transitions (hf = E2 - E1)
concepts.explanation: For an electron transition between energy levels, the emitted/absorbed photon satisfies hf = E2 − E1.

concepts.name: Spectroscopy as a scientific tool
concepts.explanation: Using spectra to identify substances and infer physical conditions by analysing spectral lines and continuous spectra.

concepts.name: Line spectra vs continuous spectra
concepts.explanation: Distinguishing discrete line spectra (from atoms) from continuous spectra (from hot dense sources) based on spectral distribution.

concepts.name: Ionising radiation health hazards
concepts.explanation: General health risks associated with exposure to ionising radiation (e.g., tissue damage and increased cancer risk).

concepts.name: Factors affecting biological impact of ionising radiation
concepts.explanation: The effect of ionising radiation on humans depends on radiation type, source activity (in Bq), exposure time, and the type of tissue irradiated.

concepts.name: Activity of a radioactive source (Becquerel, Bq)
concepts.explanation: Radioactive activity is the rate of nuclear decays in a source, measured in becquerels (1 Bq = 1 decay per second).

concepts.name: X-rays as ionising radiation
concepts.explanation: X-rays are high-energy electromagnetic radiation capable of ionising atoms and causing biological damage.

concepts.name: Nuclear radiation as ionising radiation
concepts.explanation: Radiation emitted from nuclear processes (e.g., alpha, beta, gamma) that can ionise matter and affect living tissue.

concepts.name: Environmental radiation exposure
concepts.explanation: Exposure to ionising radiation from the environment and the associated consideration of its effects on humans.

concepts.name: Conservation of energy in nuclear reactions
concepts.explanation: Apply energy conservation to nuclear processes, including accounting for reaction energy release (Q-value).
concepts.broader_concept: Conservation laws in nuclear and particle interactions

concepts.name: Conservation of momentum in nuclear reactions
concepts.explanation: Use momentum conservation to analyze nuclear reactions and decays; missing momentum indicates an unobserved particle.
concepts.broader_concept: Conservation laws in nuclear and particle interactions

concepts.name: Mass–energy equivalence (E=mc^2)
concepts.explanation: Relate changes in mass to changes in energy in nuclear and particle reactions using E=mc^2.
concepts.broader_concept: Relativistic energy and mass in particle processes

concepts.name: Q-value (reaction energy) in nuclear reactions
concepts.explanation: Calculate and interpret the Q-value as the net energy released/absorbed from mass differences between reactants and products.

concepts.name: Cockcroft–Walton experiment (artificial nuclear splitting)
concepts.explanation: Outline the first artificial splitting of a nucleus using accelerated protons (e.g., H + Li → He + He + Q) and note energy gain.

concepts.name: Acceleration of protons in particle accelerators
concepts.explanation: Describe how protons are accelerated to high kinetic energies for nuclear reactions and particle production.

concepts.name: Circular particle accelerators (synchrotron concept)
concepts.explanation: Explain the idea of circular accelerators that progressively increase particle energy to enable high-energy collisions.

concepts.name: Proton–proton collisions and particle production threshold
concepts.explanation: Relate higher collision energy to the creation of additional particles in p–p interactions (particle production).

concepts.name: Radioactive beta decay and the neutrino hypothesis
concepts.explanation: Explain that if energy/momentum appear not conserved in beta decay, an additional particle (neutrino) accounts for the missing quantities.

concepts.name: Pair production (gamma to electron–positron)
concepts.explanation: Describe conversion of energy into mass via γ → e⁺ + e⁻ with conservation of charge and momentum.

concepts.name: Electron–positron annihilation to gamma rays
concepts.explanation: Describe e⁺ + e⁻ → 2γ and apply conservation of charge and momentum in annihilation.

concepts.name: Antimatter and antiparticles
concepts.explanation: Define antimatter as particles with corresponding antiparticles (same mass, opposite charge and other quantum numbers).

concepts.name: Fundamental forces of nature (overview)
concepts.explanation: Identify the four fundamental interactions (strong, weak, electromagnetic, gravitational) and the types of particles they act on.

concepts.name: Strong nuclear force (short range, binding nuclei)
concepts.explanation: Describe the strong interaction as a short-range force responsible for binding nucleons in the nucleus.

concepts.name: Weak nuclear force (short range, non-strong-interacting particles)
concepts.explanation: Describe the weak interaction as short-range and responsible for processes involving particles not subject to the strong force (e.g., beta decay).

concepts.name: Electromagnetic force between charges (inverse-square law)
concepts.explanation: State that the electromagnetic interaction acts between charged particles and decreases with distance according to an inverse-square law.

concepts.name: Gravitational force (inverse-square law)
concepts.explanation: State that gravitational attraction follows an inverse-square dependence on separation (noting its relative weakness at particle scales).

concepts.name: Families of particles: leptons
concepts.explanation: Classify leptons as point-like particles not subject to the strong force (e.g., electron, positron, neutrino).

concepts.name: Families of particles: baryons
concepts.explanation: Classify baryons as strongly interacting particles such as protons and neutrons (and heavier baryons).

concepts.name: Families of particles: mesons
concepts.explanation: Classify mesons as strongly interacting particles with masses between electron and proton (e.g., pion), composed of quark–antiquark pairs.

concepts.name: Quark model (baryons and mesons composition)
concepts.explanation: Describe hadrons as composite particles: baryons made of three quarks and mesons made of a quark–antiquark pair.

concepts.name: Six quark flavors
concepts.explanation: Name the six quark flavors: up, down, strange, charm, top, bottom.

concepts.name: Quark electric charges (u=+2/3, d/s=-1/3)
concepts.explanation: Use fractional quark charges to determine the total charge of hadrons from their quark content.

concepts.name: Antiquarks (opposite charge, same mass)
concepts.explanation: Define antiquarks as having opposite charge to corresponding quarks while sharing the same mass.

concepts.name: Proton quark composition (uud)
concepts.explanation: Identify the proton as a baryon composed of two up quarks and one down quark (uud).

concepts.name: Neutron quark composition (udd)
concepts.explanation: Identify the neutron as a baryon composed of one up quark and two down quarks (udd).

concepts.name: Applied electricity
concepts.explanation: Practical application of electrical principles in real-world systems such as wiring, circuits, and electrical devices.

concepts.name: Electromagnetic induction (Faraday's law)
concepts.explanation: Induced emf is produced when magnetic flux through a circuit changes; magnitude relates to the rate of change of flux.

concepts.name: Solenoid magnetic field and current
concepts.explanation: A current-carrying solenoid produces a magnetic field similar to a bar magnet; field strength depends on current, turns per unit length, and core material.

concepts.name: Alternating current (AC) basics
concepts.explanation: AC is an electric current that reverses direction periodically; described by frequency, period, and peak/rms values.

concepts.name: Rectification using a p-n diode (half-wave rectifier)
concepts.explanation: A single diode allows current in one direction only, converting AC to a pulsating DC output by removing one half-cycle.

concepts.name: Bridge rectifier (full-wave rectification)
concepts.explanation: A four-diode bridge rectifier converts AC to pulsating DC using both half-cycles, producing a higher average DC output than half-wave rectification.

concepts.name: Smoothing DC using a capacitor filter
concepts.explanation: A capacitor connected after a rectifier reduces ripple by charging near peaks and discharging between peaks to maintain a steadier DC output.

concepts.name: Transformer efficiency factors
concepts.explanation: Transformer efficiency is reduced by copper losses, eddy currents, hysteresis, and flux leakage; improved by laminated cores and suitable materials.

concepts.name: Simple AC generator principle
concepts.explanation: An AC generator produces alternating emf by rotating a coil in a magnetic field (or rotating a magnet near a coil), relying on electromagnetic induction.

concepts.name: Induction motor principle
concepts.explanation: An induction motor operates via a rotating magnetic field inducing currents in the rotor; interaction of induced currents with the magnetic field produces torque.

concepts.name: Simple DC motor operation
concepts.explanation: A DC motor converts electrical energy to mechanical rotation using the motor effect, with commutation maintaining torque in a consistent direction.

concepts.name: Moving-coil galvanometer principle
concepts.explanation: A moving-coil galvanometer measures small currents using torque on a current-carrying coil in a magnetic field opposed by a restoring spring.

concepts.name: Conversion of galvanometer to ammeter
concepts.explanation: A galvanometer is converted to an ammeter by adding a low-resistance shunt in parallel to allow measurement of larger currents.

concepts.name: Conversion of galvanometer to voltmeter
concepts.explanation: A galvanometer is converted to a voltmeter by adding a high resistance in series to measure potential difference with minimal circuit disturbance.

concepts.name: Transistor as an electronic switch (relay switching)
concepts.explanation: A transistor can control a larger current using a smaller input signal, enabling switching of devices such as electromagnetic relays.

concepts.name: NOT gate implementation using a transistor
concepts.explanation: A transistor inverter produces an output logic level opposite to the input by using transistor cutoff/saturation in a simple switching circuit.

concepts.name: Truth tables for AND, OR, and NOT gates
concepts.explanation: Truth tables enumerate all input combinations and corresponding outputs for basic logic gates, forming the basis for digital circuit analysis.

concepts.name: Electromagnetic relay operation
concepts.explanation: A relay uses an electromagnet to open or close contacts, allowing a low-power circuit to control a higher-power circuit electrically.

concepts.name: Moving-coil loudspeaker principle
concepts.explanation: A loudspeaker converts electrical signals to sound by varying the force on a voice coil in a magnetic field, driving a cone to create pressure waves.

concepts.name: LED as an optical display device
concepts.explanation: A light-emitting diode produces light when forward biased due to electron-hole recombination, enabling indicator and display applications.

concepts.name: Light-emitting diode (LED) principle of operation
concepts.explanation: Explains how an LED emits light when forward-biased due to electron–hole recombination in a p–n junction, converting electrical energy to photons.

concepts.name: Photodiode operation
concepts.explanation: Describes how a photodiode converts incident light into an electrical signal via photon-generated charge carriers in a semiconductor junction (typically operated in reverse bias).

concepts.name: Basic structure of a bipolar junction transistor (BJT)
concepts.explanation: Identifies the three regions (emitter, base, collector) and the two junctions of an NPN/PNP transistor and their roles in transistor action.

concepts.name: Transistor as a voltage amplifier
concepts.explanation: Uses a transistor circuit to produce a larger output voltage variation from a smaller input signal by controlling collector current and voltage across a load.

concepts.name: Bias resistor purpose in transistor amplifier circuits
concepts.explanation: Explains how biasing sets a stable operating point (Q-point) so the transistor remains in the active region for faithful amplification.

concepts.name: Load resistor purpose in transistor amplifier circuits
concepts.explanation: Explains how a load resistor converts changes in transistor current into changes in output voltage (signal output) and helps set gain and output swing.

concepts.name: Transistor as a voltage inverter
concepts.explanation: Describes using a transistor switching configuration where an increase in input drives the output low (inverts logic level) and vice versa.

concepts.name: AND gate logic function
concepts.explanation: Defines the digital logic operation where the output is true/high only when all inputs are true/high.

concepts.name: OR gate logic function
concepts.explanation: Defines the digital logic operation where the output is true/high when at least one input is true/high.

concepts.name: NOT gate logic function
concepts.explanation: Defines the digital logic operation that outputs the logical inverse of the input (inverter).

concepts.name: Light-emitting diode (LED)
concepts.explanation: A semiconductor diode that emits light when forward biased, due to electron-hole recombination releasing energy as photons (electroluminescence).

concepts.name: Proton
concepts.explanation: A positively charged baryon found in atomic nuclei; symbol p.

concepts.name: Neutron
concepts.explanation: An electrically neutral baryon found in atomic nuclei; symbol n.

concepts.name: Positron
concepts.explanation: The electron’s antiparticle with the same mass and positive charge; symbol e+.

concepts.name: Neutrino
concepts.explanation: A nearly massless, electrically neutral lepton that interacts weakly; symbol ν.

concepts.name: Quark flavors
concepts.explanation: The six types of quarks: up (u), down (d), strange (s), charmed (c), top (t), bottom (b).

concepts.name: Antiquarks
concepts.explanation: Antiparticles of quarks corresponding to each flavor (u, d, s, c, t, b) with opposite quantum numbers.

concepts.name: Kelvin temperature scale
concepts.explanation: Use of kelvin (K) as the SI unit for thermodynamic temperature.

concepts.name: Electronvolt (eV) as an energy unit
concepts.explanation: Non-SI energy unit used in atomic and modern physics to express small energy changes.

concepts.name: Temperature (T)
concepts.explanation: Temperature as a physical quantity represented by the symbol T, measured in the SI unit kelvin (K).

concepts.name: Kelvin (K)
concepts.explanation: The SI base unit of thermodynamic temperature, symbol K.

concepts.name: Degree Celsius (°C)
concepts.explanation: A commonly used temperature unit, symbol °C, related to kelvin by an additive offset.

concepts.name: Temperature symbol t (Celsius)
concepts.explanation: Use of the symbol t to denote temperature measured in degrees Celsius (°C).

concepts.name: Temperature symbol θ (Celsius)
concepts.explanation: Use of the symbol θ to denote temperature measured in degrees Celsius (°C).

concepts.name: Temperature change (Δθ)
concepts.explanation: Difference between final and initial temperature; Δθ = θ_final − θ_initial, used to quantify heating or cooling.

concepts.name: Heat energy (Q)
concepts.explanation: Thermal energy transferred between systems due to a temperature difference, commonly denoted by Q in calculations.

concepts.name: Joule (J) as the unit of heat energy
concepts.explanation: The SI unit of energy (including heat), where heat energy Q is measured in joules (J).
concepts.broader_concept: Units and Measurement of Thermal Quantities

concepts.name: Heat Capacity Symbol (C)
concepts.explanation: Standard symbol C used to represent heat capacity in formulas relating heat energy to temperature change.

concepts.name: Unit of Heat Capacity (J K^-1)
concepts.explanation: The SI unit of heat capacity is joule per kelvin (J K^-1), indicating energy needed per kelvin temperature rise.

concepts.name: Specific heat capacity (c)
concepts.explanation: Material property defined as the heat energy required to raise the temperature of 1 kg of a substance by 1 K; commonly used in the relation Q = mcΔT.

concepts.name: Unit of specific heat capacity: J kg^-1 K^-1
concepts.explanation: SI unit for specific heat capacity, indicating joules of energy per kilogram per kelvin temperature change.

concepts.name: Unit conversion for specific heat capacity: kJ kg^-1 K^-1
concepts.explanation: Expression of specific heat capacity using kilojoules instead of joules, requiring conversion by a factor of 1000 between kJ and J.

concepts.name: Latent heat (L)
concepts.explanation: Heat absorbed or released during a change of state at constant temperature, commonly denoted by L.

concepts.name: Joule (J) as the unit of heat/energy
concepts.explanation: The SI unit used to measure heat and energy; 1 joule (J) is the standard unit for thermal energy transfer.
concepts.broader_concept: Units and Measurement in Thermal Physics

concepts.name: Frequency
concepts.explanation: Number of oscillations or wave cycles per second; SI unit hertz (Hz).

concepts.name: Amplitude
concepts.explanation: Maximum displacement of a wave or oscillation from its equilibrium position; measured in metres (m) for displacement waves.

concepts.name: Tension in a wire
concepts.explanation: Pulling force along a stretched wire/string that affects wave speed; SI unit newton (N).

concepts.name: Mass per unit length
concepts.explanation: Linear density of a wire/string (μ), equal to mass divided by length; SI unit kg m^-1.

concepts.name: Focal length
concepts.explanation: Distance from the lens/mirror to its principal focus; SI unit metre (m).

concepts.name: Object distance
concepts.explanation: Distance from the object to a lens/mirror (often denoted u); SI unit metre (m).
concepts.broader_concept: Image Formation by Lenses and Mirrors

concepts.name: Image distance
concepts.explanation: Distance from the image to a lens/mirror (often denoted v); SI unit metre (m).
concepts.broader_concept: Image Formation by Lenses and Mirrors

concepts.name: Magnification
concepts.explanation: Ratio of image size to object size (or image distance to object distance with sign convention); dimensionless.
concepts.broader_concept: Image Formation by Lenses and Mirrors

concepts.name: Angle of incidence
concepts.explanation: Angle between the incident ray and the normal to the surface at the point of incidence; commonly measured in degrees.

concepts.name: Angle of reflection
concepts.explanation: Angle between the reflected ray and the normal to the surface; equals the angle of incidence for specular reflection.

concepts.name: Angle of refraction
concepts.explanation: Angle between the refracted ray and the normal in the second medium; used in Snell's law.

concepts.name: Diffraction grating spacing
concepts.explanation: Distance between adjacent slits/lines in a diffraction grating (d); SI unit metre (m).

concepts.name: Double-slit separation
concepts.explanation: Distance between two slits (d) in a two-slit interference setup; SI unit metre (m).

concepts.name: Atomic number (Z)
concepts.explanation: The number of protons in the nucleus of an atom; identifies the element.

concepts.name: Mass number (A)
concepts.explanation: The total number of nucleons (protons + neutrons) in the nucleus of an atom.

concepts.name: Electronic charge (e)
concepts.explanation: The elementary charge, i.e., the magnitude of the charge carried by a single electron/proton; used as a fundamental constant in atomic-scale calculations.

concepts.name: Planck constant (h)
concepts.explanation: A fundamental constant relating energy to frequency for photons via E = hf; central to quantum descriptions of atomic phenomena.

concepts.name: Activity of a radioactive source
concepts.explanation: The rate of radioactive decays per unit time; measured in becquerels (Bq).

concepts.name: Radioactive decay constant (λ)
concepts.explanation: The probability per unit time that a nucleus will decay; relates to activity and half-life (e.g., A = λN).

concepts.name: Half-life (T1/2)
concepts.explanation: The time taken for the number of undecayed nuclei (or activity) to fall to half its initial value.

concepts.name: Photovoltaic cell
concepts.explanation: A p–n junction device that converts incident light into electrical energy by generating a photovoltage and photocurrent (photovoltaic effect).

concepts.name: Diode/rectifier
concepts.explanation: A p–n junction diode used to allow current in one direction, commonly converting AC to pulsating DC (rectification).

concepts.name: p–n junction transistor
concepts.explanation: A bipolar junction transistor (BJT) made of two p–n junctions, used for amplification or switching by controlling collector current via a small base current.

concepts.name: PNP junction transistor
concepts.explanation: A BJT with p–n–p layers in which holes are the majority carriers; operation depends on biasing emitter-base and collector-base junctions.

concepts.name: NPN junction transistor
concepts.explanation: A BJT with n–p–n layers in which electrons are the majority carriers; widely used for amplification and switching with appropriate junction biasing.

concepts.name: Photodiode
concepts.explanation: A semiconductor light sensor that converts incident light into an electrical signal, typically by generating a photocurrent when operated under reverse bias.

concepts.name: Light-sensitive diode
concepts.explanation: A diode designed to respond to light by changing its electrical behavior (e.g., producing a photocurrent or changing resistance), commonly implemented as a photodiode.

concepts.name: NOT gate (inverter)
concepts.explanation: A digital logic gate that outputs the opposite logic level to its input (0→1, 1→0).

concepts.name: AND gate
concepts.explanation: A digital logic gate that outputs 1 only when all inputs are 1; otherwise outputs 0.

concepts.name: OR gate
concepts.explanation: A digital logic gate that outputs 1 when at least one input is 1; outputs 0 only when all inputs are 0.

concepts.name: Momentum of a particle
concepts.explanation: Linear momentum defined as the product of mass and velocity: p = mv.

concepts.name: Conservation of linear momentum (two-body collisions)
concepts.explanation: Total momentum before interaction equals total momentum after: m1u1 + m2u2 = m1v1 + m2v2.

concepts.name: Radian measure of angle
concepts.explanation: Angle in radians defined by arc length divided by radius: θ = s/r.

concepts.name: Relation between linear speed and angular speed
concepts.explanation: For circular motion, tangential speed is proportional to angular speed: v = rω.

concepts.name: Centripetal acceleration
concepts.explanation: Acceleration directed toward the center of circular motion: a = rω^2 (equivalently a = v^2/r).

concepts.name: Weight as gravitational force near Earth
concepts.explanation: Weight defined as the gravitational force on a mass: W = mg.

concepts.name: Gravitational field strength from orbital period
concepts.explanation: Using orbital/pendulum relation to determine g from period: g = 4π^2l/T^2 (as indicated by g = … T^2 = …).

concepts.name: Pressure as force per unit area
concepts.explanation: Definition of pressure: p = F/A.

concepts.name: Hydrostatic pressure in a fluid
concepts.explanation: Pressure at depth in a fluid: p = ρgh.

concepts.name: Couple (moment of a couple)
concepts.explanation: Two equal and opposite forces separated by distance produce a turning effect: couple torque T = Fd.

concepts.name: Simple harmonic motion (acceleration relation)
concepts.explanation: In SHM, acceleration is proportional to displacement and directed toward equilibrium: a = −ω^2s.

concepts.name: Period-frequency relationship
concepts.explanation: Time period and frequency are reciprocals: T = 1/f.

concepts.name: Angular frequency relationship
concepts.explanation: Connection between angular frequency and period/frequency: ω = 2πf = 2π/T.

concepts.name: Time period of a simple pendulum
concepts.explanation: For small oscillations, period depends on length and g: T = 2π√(l/g).

concepts.name: Work done by a constant force
concepts.explanation: Work equals force times displacement in the direction of the force: W = Fs.

concepts.name: Kinetic energy
concepts.explanation: Energy of motion: Ek = (1/2)mv^2.

concepts.name: Power
concepts.explanation: Rate of doing work or energy transfer: P = W/t.

concepts.name: Absolute zero offset (273.15 K)
concepts.explanation: The numerical offset between the Celsius and Kelvin scales, reflecting that 0 °C corresponds to 273.15 K.

concepts.name: Heat energy needed for a change of state
concepts.explanation: The amount of heat energy required to change a substance from one physical state to another (e.g., melting or boiling) without changing its temperature (latent heat concept).

concepts.name: Heat transfer equation (Q = mcΔθ)
concepts.explanation: Formula for the heat absorbed or released by a substance: Q equals mass times specific heat capacity times temperature change (Δθ).

concepts.name: Heat transfer equation using heat capacity (Q = CΔθ)
concepts.explanation: Formula relating heat transfer Q to an object's heat capacity C and its temperature change (Δθ).

concepts.name: Latent heat formula (Q = mL)
concepts.explanation: Heat energy required for a change of state without temperature change is given by Q = mL, where m is mass and L is specific latent heat.
concepts.broader_concept: Latent Heat and Change of State

concepts.name: Latent heat (heat of change of state)
concepts.explanation: Energy absorbed or released during a phase change at constant temperature (e.g., melting, boiling).
concepts.broader_concept: Latent Heat and Change of State

concepts.name: Specific latent heat (L)
concepts.explanation: Amount of heat energy required per unit mass to change the state of a substance (units: J/kg).
concepts.broader_concept: Latent Heat and Change of State

concepts.name: Wave speed relationship (c = fλ)
concepts.explanation: Relates wave speed to frequency and wavelength: c = fλ.

concepts.name: Doppler effect for waves (moving observer/source)
concepts.explanation: Observed frequency changes due to relative motion; commonly expressed using f' = f c/(c ± u) for motion along the line of sight.

concepts.name: Thin lens equation (1/f = 1/u + 1/v)
concepts.explanation: Relates focal length to object distance u and image distance v for a thin lens: 1/f = 1/u + 1/v.

concepts.name: Magnification of a lens (m = v/u)
concepts.explanation: Linear magnification is the ratio of image distance to object distance: m = v/u (sign conventions may apply).

concepts.name: Lens power (P = 1/f)
concepts.explanation: Optical power of a lens is the reciprocal of focal length (in metres): P = 1/f, measured in dioptres.

concepts.name: Equivalent power of lenses in contact (P = P1 + P2)
concepts.explanation: For thin lenses in contact, total power equals the sum of individual powers: Ptotal = P1 + P2.

concepts.name: Refractive index definition (n = sin i / sin r)
concepts.explanation: Defines refractive index using Snell's law: n = sin i / sin r for light passing from air into a medium.

concepts.name: Refractive index as speed ratio (n = c1/c2)
concepts.explanation: Refractive index equals the ratio of light speeds in two media: n = c1/c2 (often c/v when c is speed in vacuum).

concepts.name: Real and apparent depth relationship
concepts.explanation: Relates real depth to apparent depth when viewing into a refracting medium; commonly real depth/apparent depth = n (for small angles from air).

concepts.name: Coulomb’s law
concepts.explanation: Electrostatic force between two point charges is proportional to the product of the charges and inversely proportional to the square of their separation (F = kq1q2/r^2).

concepts.name: Electric field strength
concepts.explanation: Definition of electric field at a point as force per unit positive test charge (E = F/q).

concepts.name: Potential difference
concepts.explanation: Definition of potential difference between two points as energy transferred (work done) per unit charge (V = W/q).

concepts.name: Ohm’s law
concepts.explanation: Relationship between potential difference, current, and resistance for an ohmic conductor (V = IR).

concepts.name: Capacitance
concepts.explanation: Ability of a capacitor to store charge per unit potential difference (C = Q/V).

concepts.name: Parallel-plate capacitor capacitance
concepts.explanation: Capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor depends on permittivity, plate area, and separation (C = εA/d).

concepts.name: Resistivity
concepts.explanation: Material property relating resistance to dimensions, defined by ρ = RA/L (equivalently R = ρL/A).

concepts.name: Resistors in series (equivalent resistance)
concepts.explanation: For series connection, total resistance is the sum of individual resistances (R_total = R1 + R2 + ...).

concepts.name: Resistors in parallel (equivalent resistance)
concepts.explanation: For parallel connection, reciprocals add: 1/R_total = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + ... .

concepts.name: Joule's law of heating
concepts.explanation: Electrical energy converted to heat in a resistor: W = I^2 R t.

concepts.name: Electric power in a circuit
concepts.explanation: Rate of electrical energy transfer: P = VI (also consistent with Joule heating in resistors).
concepts.broader_concept: Electric power and energy in circuits

concepts.name: Magnetic flux
concepts.explanation: Magnetic flux through an area: Φ = B A (for uniform field normal to the area).

concepts.name: Magnetic force on a moving charged particle
concepts.explanation: Lorentz magnetic force magnitude for perpendicular motion: F = q v B.
concepts.broader_concept: Motion of charges in magnetic fields

concepts.name: Induced electromotive force (Faraday's law idea)
concepts.explanation: An emf is induced when magnetic flux linked with a circuit changes (basis of electromagnetic induction).

concepts.name: Transformer principle
concepts.explanation: Uses changing magnetic flux to induce emf in a secondary coil, enabling step-up/step-down of AC voltage.

concepts.name: RMS value of alternating voltage and current
concepts.explanation: Effective values used for AC power calculations: Vrms and Irms (root-mean-square).

concepts.name: Einstein photoelectric equation (hf = Φ + K_max)
concepts.explanation: In the photoelectric effect, photon energy equals the work function Φ plus the maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons (K_max = 1/2 mv_max^2).

concepts.name: Law of radioactive decay (dN/dt = -λN)
concepts.explanation: Radioactive decay rate is proportional to the number of undecayed nuclei N; λ is the decay constant.

concepts.name: Half-life and decay constant relationship (T1/2 = ln 2 / λ)
concepts.explanation: Half-life T1/2 is the time for the number of undecayed nuclei to fall to half its initial value and is related to λ by T1/2 = ln(2)/λ.

concepts.name: Mass-energy equivalence (E = mc^2)
concepts.explanation: Rest energy of a mass m is E = mc^2, expressing equivalence between mass and energy.
